ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ يُدْخِلْهُ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَذَلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ) (١٣ (وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَيَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَهُ يُدْخِلْهُ نَارًا خَالِدًا فِيهَا وَلَهُ عَذَابٌ مُهِينٌ) (١٤).
His saying: (يُدْخِلْهُ): in both verses it is read with yāʾ and with nūn, and their meaning is the same. (نَارًا خَالِدًا فِيهَا): نَارًا is the second object of يُدْخِلُ, and خَالِدًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the first object.
It may not be an adjective (ṣifa) of نَار, because if it were so, the pronoun of the agent would have to be made overt, since it would then be applied to something other than the one it belongs to. On the view of the Kufans, making it an adjective comes out as permissible, because they do not require the pronoun to be made overt in this kind of construction.

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاللَّاتِي يَأْتِينَ الْفَاحِشَةَ مِنْ نِسَائِكُمْ فَاسْتَشْهِدُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ أَرْبَعَةً مِنْكُمْ فَإِنْ شَهِدُوا فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ فِي الْبُيُوتِ حَتَّى يَتَوَفَّاهُنَّ الْمَوْتُ أَوْ يَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ لَهُنَّ سَبِيلًا) (١٥).
His saying: (وَاللَّاتِي): it is the plural of «الَّتِي», formed irregularly. It is also said: it is a form coined for the plural. Its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). The khabar (predicate) is فَاسْتَشْهِدُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ; this is permitted even though it is a command, because it has taken on the status of a conditional, since الَّتِي has been joined to a verb as its ṣila (relative clause). That being so, the accusative is not good, because implying the verb before the conditional particle is not permissible, and implying it after the ṣila would require supplying a verb other than his saying «فَاسْتَشْهِدُوا», because اسْتَشْهِدُوا cannot properly govern the accusative in اللَّاتِي; and there is no need for that when the mubtadaʾ reading is sound. Some permitted the accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "aim at (اقْصُدُوا) اللَّاتِي" or "intend (تَعَمَّدُوا)". It is also said: the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "and among what is recited to you is the ruling on اللَّاتِي". So "among what is recited" is the khabar and "ruling" is the mubtadaʾ; both were omitted because his saying «فَاسْتَشْهِدُوا» points to them, since it is the ruling recited to them. (أَوْ يَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ): أَوْ is a conjunction, and the implied form is "or until Allah makes". It is also said: it means "unless" (إِلَّا أَنْ); both are sound. (لَهُنَّ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَجْعَلَ», or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «سَبِيلًا».

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاللَّذَانِ يَأْتِيَانِهَا مِنْكُمْ فَآذُوهُمَا فَإِنْ تَابَا وَأَصْلَحَا فَأَعْرِضُوا عَنْهُمَا إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ تَوَّابًا رَحِيمًا) (٦). [Translator's note: the verse number appears in the source as (٦); this is verse 16.]
His saying: (وَاللَّذَانِ يَأْتِيَانِهَا): what is said about اللَّذَانِ is like what is said about اللَّاتِي, except that whoever permits the accusative can properly imply a verb of the same kind as the one mentioned; its implied form being "harm (آذُوا) اللَّذَيْنِ".
What comes after the fāʾ may not govern what precedes it here, even if it were stripped of the object pronoun, because the fāʾ here has the status of the fāʾ that occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and that cuts off what follows it from what precedes it. اللَّذَانِ is read with the nūn light, according to the basic form of the dual, and with it doubled, on the basis that one of the two nūns is a compensation for the omitted lām, since the original is اللَّذَيَانِ, like الْعَمَيَانِ and الشَّجَيَانِ; the yāʾ was dropped because the noun is vague (mubham), and vague nouns are not given the regular, morphological dual; the dropping signals that the dual here departs from the norm. It is also said: it was dropped because of the length the phrase acquires through the ṣila. As for هَذَانِ, هَاتَيْنِ and فَذَانِكَ, we will mention them in their places.

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّمَا التَّوْبَةُ عَلَى اللَّهِ لِلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السُّوءَ بِجَهَالَةٍ ثُمَّ يَتُوبُونَ مِنْ قَرِيبٍ فَأُولَئِكَ يَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا) (١٧).
His saying: (إِنَّمَا التَّوْبَةُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and there are two views on the khabar (predicate). First: it is (عَلَى اللَّهِ), i.e. "established upon Allah"; on this view «لِلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السُّوءَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the adverbial phrase, namely his saying «عَلَى اللَّهِ», and what governs it is the adverbial phrase or the notion of settledness (al-istiqrār), i.e. "being for those who…". The governor of the ḥāl may not be التَّوْبَةُ, because the preposition phrase has separated them. The second view: the khabar is «لِلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ»; as for «عَلَى اللَّهِ», it is a ḥāl from something omitted, its implied form being "repentance, since it is upon Allah", or "when it is upon Allah"; so إِذْ or إِذَا are two adverbs governed by الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السُّوءَ, because an adverb may be governed by a meaning even if it precedes it. And kāna is the complete (tāmma) kāna, and the owner of the ḥāl is the agent pronoun in kāna. «عَلَى اللَّهِ» may not be a ḥāl governed by الَّذِينَ, because that is an abstract (maʿnawī) governor, and the ḥāl does not precede an abstract governor. The parallel of this question is their saying هَذَا بُسْرًا أَطْيَبُ مِنْهُ رُطَبًا ("this, as unripe dates, is better than it as ripe dates").

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَيْسَتِ التَّوْبَةُ لِلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السَّيِّئَاتِ حَتَّى إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَهُمُ الْمَوْتُ قَالَ إِنِّي تُبْتُ الْآنَ وَلَا الَّذِينَ يَمُوتُونَ وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ أُولَئِكَ أَعْتَدْنَا لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا) (١٨).
His saying: (وَلَا الَّذِينَ يَمُوتُونَ): there are two views on its position. First: it is genitive, conjoined to الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السَّيِّئَاتِ, i.e. "nor for those who die". The second view: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate) is «أُولَئِكَ أَعْتَدْنَا لَهُمْ». And the lām is the lām of the mubtadaʾ (lām al-ibtidāʾ), not the negating lā. [Translator's note: so in the source; the reading meant is presumably وَلَلَّذِينَ, with the lām of the mubtadaʾ, as opposed to the canonical وَلَا الَّذِينَ.]

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَرِثُوا النِّسَاءَ كَرْهًا وَلَا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ لِتَذْهَبُوا بِبَعْضِ مَا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ إِلَّا أَنْ يَأْتِينَ بِفَاحِشَةٍ مُبَيِّنَةٍ وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ فَإِنْ كَرِهْتُمُوهُنَّ فَعَسَى أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئًا وَيَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ فِيهِ خَيْرًا كَثِيرًا) (١٩).
His saying: (أَنْ تَرِثُوا): in the nominative position as the fāʿil (agent) of يَحِلُّ. «النِّسَاءَ» has two views. First: it is the first object, and on this view the women are the ones inherited; the people of the Jāhiliyya used to inherit their fathers' wives, saying, "We have more right to marry them." Second: it is the second object, the implied form being "that you inherit wealth from the women".
(كَرْهًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object; it has ḍamma and fatḥa, and this was mentioned in Āl ʿImrān. (وَلَا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ): there are two views. First: it is accusative, conjoined to تَرِثُوا, i.e. "nor that you hinder them". Second: it is jussive by the prohibition, and so it is a fresh (resumptive) clause. (لِتَذْهَبُوا): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to تَعْضُلُوا, and there is an ellipsis in the phrase, its implied form being "and do not hinder them from marriage" or "from divorce", according to their disagreement over who is addressed by it: the guardians or the husbands. (مَا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ): the pronoun referring back to مَا is omitted, its implied form being "what you gave them of it (إِيَّاهُ)", and it is the second object. (إِلَّا أَنْ يَأْتِينَ بِفَاحِشَةٍ): there are two views. First: it is in the accusative position as a disjoined (munqaṭiʿ) exception. Second: it is in the position of a ḥāl, its implied form being "except in the state of their committing the indecency". It is also said: it is a joined (muttaṣil) exception, its implied form being "and do not hinder them in any state except in the state of committing indecency". (مُبَيِّنَةٍ): read with fatḥa on the yāʾ, as a passive (lit. "that whose agent is not named"), i.e. its doer made it manifest; and with kasra on the yāʾ and doubling, and in this there are two views. First: that it is the agent, i.e. it makes clear the state of the one who commits it. Second: that it is from the intransitive; one says بَانَ الشَّيْءُ, أَبَانَ, تَبَيَّنَ, اسْتَبَانَ and بَيَّنَ with one meaning ("the thing became clear"). And it is read with kasra on the bāʾ and sukūn on the yāʾ, and this is on the two views given for the doubled form with kasra. (بِالْمَعْرُوفِ): an object or a ḥāl. (أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا): the fāʿil of عَسَى, and it has no khabar (predicate) here, because when the maṣdar comes first, عَسَى takes the meaning of "it is near" (قَرُبَ), and so it does without the implied object that is called the khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنْ أَرَدْتُمُ اسْتِبْدَالَ زَوْجٍ مَكَانَ زَوْجٍ وَآتَيْتُمْ إِحْدَاهُنَّ قِنْطَارًا فَلَا تَأْخُذُوا مِنْهُ شَيْئًا أَتَأْخُذُونَهُ بُهْتَانًا وَإِثْمًا مُبِينًا) (٢٠).
His saying: (وَإِنْ أَرَدْتُمُ اسْتِبْدَالَ زَوْجٍ مَكَانَ زَوْجٍ): [Translator's note: the comment refers to مَكَانَ.] an adverb (ẓarf) for الِاسْتِبْدَال.
In his saying (وَآتَيْتُمْ إِحْدَاهُنَّ قِنْطَارًا) there are two difficulties. First: that he made the pronoun plural while what preceded is two spouses. Second: that the one he wishes to exchange is the one to whom he has already given wealth, so he is forbidden from taking it back; as for the one he wishes to take anew, he had not given her anything for him to be forbidden from taking it. This is supported by his saying: «وَكَيْفَ تَأْخُذُونَهُ وَقَدْ أَفْضَى بَعْضُكُمْ إِلَى بَعْضٍ». The answer to the first is that what is meant by "spouse" is the plural, because the address is to the group of men, and each of them may wish to make an exchange. It may also be plural because the one he wishes to take anew will end up being a wife, and he may wish to exchange her as he exchanged the first, so it was made plural on this meaning.
As for the second difficulty, there are two answers. First: that he put the overt noun in place of the pronoun, the original being آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ. Second: that the one being exchanged is indeterminate, so he said إِحْدَاهُنَّ, since she was not specified for the pronoun to refer back to her. We have mentioned something like this in his saying: (فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَاهُمَا الْأُخْرَى). (بُهْتَانًا): of the pattern fuʿlān, from al-baht; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it may be a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose).

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَيْفَ تَأْخُذُونَهُ وَقَدْ أَفْضَى بَعْضُكُمْ إِلَى بَعْضٍ وَأَخَذْنَ مِنْكُمْ مِيثَاقًا غَلِيظًا) (٢١).
His saying: (وَكَيْفَ تَأْخُذُونَهُ): كَيْفَ is in the accusative position as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the implied form is "do you take it, being unjust?". This becomes clear to you from the answer to كَيْفَ: do you not see that if you said "how did you take Zayd's property?", the answer would be a ḥāl, its implied form being "I took it unjustly" or "justly", and the like? And the position of كَيْفَ is always the same as the position of its answer. (وَقَدْ أَفْضَى): also in the position of a ḥāl. (وَأَخَذْنَ): i.e. "and they have (قَدْ) taken", because it is a conjoined ḥāl and the verb is past, so قَدْ is implied with it so that it becomes a ḥāl, and its earlier mention made it unnecessary to mention it. (مِنْكُمْ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَخَذْنَ, and it may be a ḥāl from مِيثَاق.

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَنْكِحُوا مَا نَكَحَ آبَاؤُكُمْ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ إِلَّا مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ إِنَّهُ كَانَ فَاحِشَةً وَمَقْتًا وَسَاءَ سَبِيلًا) (٢٢).
His saying: (مَا نَكَحَ): like his saying (فَانْكِحُوا مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ), and likewise إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ; this recurs in the Quran. (مِنَ النِّسَاءِ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَا», or from the pronoun referring back to it. (إِلَّا مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ): in «مَا» there are two views. First: it means مَنْ ("whoever"), and this has been mentioned. Second: it is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and the exception is disjoined (munqaṭiʿ), because the prohibition concerns the future and what has passed is past, so it is not of its kind; and it is in the accusative position.
The meaning of the disjoined exception is that it is not included in the first; rather it has the status of a fresh statement, and إِلَّا in it is interpreted as لَكِنَّ ("but"). The implied form here is: "Do not marry those whom your fathers married, and do not have intercourse with those with whom your fathers had intercourse; but whatever of that has passed is pardoned", just as you say: مَا مَرَرْتُ بِرَجُلٍ إِلَّا بِامْرَأَةٍ, i.e. "but I passed by a woman". The purpose of it is to state an additional meaning: do you not see that your saying مَا مَرَرْتُ بِرَجُلٍ ("I did not pass by a man") is explicit in denying passing by any man, without touching on affirming or denying passing by a woman? So when you say إِلَّا بِامْرَأَةٍ, it is an affirmation of a meaning about which silence was kept, whose denial or affirmation was not known from the first statement.
(إِنَّهُ): the hāʾ is the pronoun of the marriage. (وَمَقْتًا): the statement is complete here, then a fresh one begins. (وَسَاءَ سَبِيلًا): i.e. "and evil is this way" of marrying those whom the fathers married. (سَبِيلًا): its tamyīz (specification). His saying «وَسَاءَ سَبِيلًا» may also be conjoined to the khabar (predicate) of kāna, the implied form being "about which it is said: evil is it as a way".

ukberi-tibyan:174-174.t:
Allah the Exalted says: {يَا أَيهَا النَّاس قد جَاءَكُم برهَان من ربكُم وأنزلنا إِلَيْكُم نورا مُبينًا}
His saying, Exalted is He: (بُرْهَانٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ): if you wish, you may make «مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ» a naʿt (adjective) of برهان, or attached (mutaʿalliq) to جاء.

ukberi-tibyan:175-175.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَاعْتَصَمُوا بِهِ فَسَيُدْخِلُهُمْ فِي رَحْمَةٍ مِنْهُ وَفَضْلٍ وَيَهْدِيهِمْ إِلَيْهِ صِرَاطًا مُسْتَقِيمًا) (١٧٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (صِرَاطًا مُسْتَقِيمًا): it is the second object of «يَهْدِي». It has also been said that it is an object of «يَهْدِي» according to the meaning, because the meaning is "He makes them know".

ukberi-tibyan:176-176.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَسْتَفْتُونَكَ قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِي الْكَلَالَةِ إِنِ امْرُؤٌ هَلَكَ لَيْسَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ وَلَهُ أُخْتٌ فَلَهَا نِصْفُ مَا تَرَكَ وَهُوَ يَرِثُهَا إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهَا وَلَدٌ فَإِنْ كَانَتَا اثْنَتَيْنِ فَلَهُمَا الثُّلُثَانِ مِمَّا تَرَكَ وَإِنْ كَانُوا إِخْوَةً رِجَالًا وَنِسَاءً فَلِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَضِلُّوا وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ) (١٧٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي الْكَلَالَةِ): «فِي» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يفتيكم. The Kufans said: to يستفتونك. This is weak, because if it were so, He would have said: يفتيكم فيها في الكلالة, just as if it had come first. (إِنِ امْرُؤٌ هَلَكَ): this is like (وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ). (لَيْسَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ): the clause is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «هَلَكَ». (وَلَهُ أُخْتٌ): a circumstantial clause as well, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is «فَلَهَا». (وَهُوَ يَرِثُهَا): resumptive, with no grammatical position, and this clause has stood in place of the apodosis of the condition, which is His saying: (إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهَا وَلَدٌ). (فَإِنْ كَانَتَا اثْنَتَيْنِ): the alif in كانتا is the pronoun of the two sisters, and what indicates that is His saying: وله أخت. It has also been said that it is the pronoun of «مَنْ», the implied form being: "if whoever inherits is two", and the pronoun of مَن has been construed according to the meaning, because it is used for the singular, dual and plural with a single form.
If it is said: it is a condition of the khabar (predicate) that it conveys what the mubtadaʾ (subject) does not convey, and the alif has already indicated two — it is answered: the benefit in His saying اثنتين is to make clear that the inheritance, which here is the two-thirds, is due by virtue of the number alone, irrespective of being young or old or anything else; for this reason it is informative. (مِمَّا تَرَكَ): in the position of a ḥāl from «الثُّلْثَانِ».
{فَإِن كَانُوا}: the pronoun refers to the heirs, and what came before indicates that.
(فَلِلذَّكَرِ): that is, of them.
(أَنْ تَضِلُّوا): there are three views on it. The first: it is the object of يبيّن, that is: He makes clear to you your going astray, so that you may know the guidance. The second: it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), its implied form being: "for fear that you go astray". The third: its implied form is: "so that you do not go astray" (لئلا تضلوا), and this is the view of the Kufans. On these [last] two views the object of يبيّن is omitted, that is: He makes the truth clear to you.

ukberi-tibyan:79-79.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَا أَصَابَكَ مِنْ حَسَنَةٍ فَمِنَ اللَّهِ وَمَا أَصَابَكَ مِنْ سَيِّئَةٍ فَمِنْ نَفْسِكَ وَأَرْسَلْنَاكَ لِلنَّاسِ رَسُولًا وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا) (٧٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا أَصَابَكَ مِنْ حَسَنَةٍ): «مَا» is conditional, and أَصَابَكَ has the meaning of يُصِيبُكَ; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is «فَمِنَ اللَّهِ».
It is not good for it to have the meaning of الَّذِي ("that which"), because that would require that what befalls them be past and specific, whereas the meaning is general; the conditional is more fitting. The implied wording is: فَهُوَ مِنَ اللَّهِ ("then it is from Allah"). What is meant in the verse is plenty and drought, and for that reason He did not say أُصِبْتَ ("you were struck"). (رَسُولًا): an emphatic ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "possessing a message". It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. إِرْسَالًا ("a sending"). لِلنَّاسِ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَرْسَلْنَا, and it may be a ḥāl from رَسُولٍ.

ukberi-tibyan:80-80.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَنْ يُطِعِ الرَّسُولَ فَقَدْ أَطَاعَ اللَّهَ وَمَنْ تَوَلَّى فَمَا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَفِيظًا) (٨٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حَفِيظًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf. عَلَيْهِمْ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to حَفِيظٍ. It may also be a ḥāl from it, in which case it is attached to something omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:81-81.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَقُولُونَ طَاعَةٌ فَإِذَا بَرَزُوا مِنْ عِنْدِكَ بَيَّتَ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْهُمْ غَيْرَ الَّذِي تَقُولُ وَاللَّهُ يَكْتُبُ مَا يُبَيِّتُونَ فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا) (٨١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (طَاعَةٌ): the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. أَمْرُنَا طَاعَةٌ ("our affair is obedience"). It may also be a mubtadaʾ, i.e. عِنْدِنَا طَاعَةٌ or مِنَّا طَاعَةٌ ("with us / from us there is obedience"). (بَيَّتَ): the basic form is that the tāʾ takes a fatḥa, because it is a past verb; the feminine tāʾ was not attached to it because الطَّائِفَة has the meaning of النَّفَر ("the group of men"). It has been read with assimilation (idghām) of the tāʾ into the ṭāʾ, on the basis that the tāʾ was made quiescent so that its assimilation would be possible, since it is from the same point of articulation as the ṭāʾ, and the ṭāʾ is stronger than it because of its elevation (istiʿlāʾ), its velarization (iṭbāq) and its voicing (jahr).
And (تَقُولُ): it may be an address to the Prophet, or it may refer to the group (al-ṭāʾifa). (مَا يُبَيِّتُونَ): «مَا» may have the meaning of الَّذِي, and be a relative noun, or be maṣdarī (forming a verbal noun).
[Translator's note: the text lists "with the meaning of الَّذِي" and "relative" as though they were two separate options.]

ukberi-tibyan:83-83.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا جَاءَهُمْ أَمْرٌ مِنَ الْأَمْنِ أَوِ الْخَوْفِ أَذَاعُوا بِهِ وَلَوْ رَدُّوهُ إِلَى الرَّسُولِ وَإِلَى أُولِي الْأَمْرِ مِنْهُمْ لَعَلِمَهُ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَنْبِطُونَهُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ لَاتَّبَعْتُمُ الشَّيْطَانَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا) (٨٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَذَاعُوا بِهِ): the alif in أَذَاعُوا is a substitute for a yāʾ; one says ذَاعَ الْأَمْرُ يَذِيعُ ("the matter spread"). The bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. أَذَاعُوهُ ("they spread it"). It is also said: it was construed according to the meaning of تَحَدَّثُوا بِهِ ("they talked about it"). (يَسْتَنْبِطُونَهُ مِنْهُمْ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الَّذِينَ or from the pronoun in يَسْتَنْبِطُونَهُ. (إِلَّا قَلِيلًا): excepted from the fāʿil (agent) of اتَّبَعْتُمْ. The meaning is: had Allah not bestowed favour upon you, you would have gone astray by following Satan, except a few of you — namely those who died in the interval between prophets (al-fatra), or those who were not legally responsible. It is also said: it is excepted from His saying أَذَاعُوا بِهِ, i.e. they made that matter or the fear public, except the few among them. It is also said: it is excepted from His saying (لَوَجَدُوا فِيهِ اخْتِلَافًا كَثِيرًا), i.e. had it been from other than Allah, they would have found contradiction in it — except the few among them, namely whoever does not examine closely.

ukberi-tibyan:84-84.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَقَاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ لَا تُكَلَّفُ إِلَّا نَفْسَكَ وَحَرِّضِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَكُفَّ بَأْسَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَاللَّهُ أَشَدُّ بَأْسًا وَأَشَدُّ تَنْكِيلًا) (٨٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَقَاتِلُوا): the fāʾ conjoins this verb to His saying (فَلْيُقَاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ); it is also said: to (وَمَا لَكُمْ لَا تُقَاتِلُونَ); and it is also said: to His saying (فَقَاتِلُوا أَوْلِيَاءَ الشَّيْطَانِ). [Translator's note: the lemma is written فَقَاتِلُوا, whereas the verse reads فَقَاتِلْ.] (لَا تُكَلَّفُ): in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (إِلَّا نَفْسَكَ): the second object. «بَأْسًا» and «تَنْكِيلًا» are tamyīz (specification).

ukberi-tibyan:85-85.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَنْ يَشْفَعْ شَفَاعَةً حَسَنَةً يَكُنْ لَهُ نَصِيبٌ مِنْهَا وَمَنْ يَشْفَعْ شَفَاعَةً سَيِّئَةً يَكُنْ لَهُ كِفْلٌ مِنْهَا وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُقِيتًا) (٨٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُقِيتًا): the yāʾ is a substitute for a wāw; it is of the pattern mufʿil, from al-qūt ("sustenance").

ukberi-tibyan:86-86.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا حُيِّيتُمْ بِتَحِيَّةٍ فَحَيُّوا بِأَحْسَنَ مِنْهَا أَوْ رُدُّوهَا إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَسِيبًا) (٨٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِتَحِيَّةٍ): its original form is تَحْيِيَةٌ, of the pattern tafʿila from حَيَيْتُ; the vowel of the yāʾ was transferred to the ḥāʾ and then it was assimilated. And (حَيُّوا): its original form is حَيَيُوا; then the yāʾ was dropped, as has been mentioned in several places. (بِأَحْسَنَ): i.e. بِتَحِيَّةٍ أَحْسَنَ ("with a better greeting"). (أَوْ رُدُّوهَا): i.e. رُدُّوا مِثْلَهَا ("return its like"); the muḍāf was omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:87-87.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ وَمَنْ أَصْدَقُ مِنَ اللَّهِ حَدِيثًا) (٨٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ): this has been discussed under the Verse of the Throne. (لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ): the response of an omitted oath; it may be resumptive with no grammatical position, and it may be another khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject). (إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ): it is said that the implied wording is فِي يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ ("on the Day of Resurrection"); it is also said that it keeps its proper meaning, i.e. "He will surely gather you in the graves", or "from the graves". On this view it may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "He will gather you, leading on to the reckoning of the Day of Resurrection". (لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ): it may be a ḥāl from يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ, with the hāʾ referring back to the Day; and it may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. جَمْعًا لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ ("a gathering in which there is no doubt"), with the hāʾ referring back to the gathering. And (حَدِيثًا): tamyīz (specification).

ukberi-tibyan:88-88.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَمَا لَكُمْ فِي الْمُنَافِقِينَ فِئَتَيْنِ وَاللَّهُ أَرْكَسَهُمْ بِمَا كَسَبُوا أَتُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَهْدُوا مَنْ أَضَلَّ اللَّهُ وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُ سَبِيلًا) (٨٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَمَا لَكُمْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). And (فِئَتَيْنِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial); what governs it is the adverbial phrase لَكُمْ, or what governs the adverbial phrase. فِي الْمُنَافِقِينَ admits two possibilities. First: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the meaning of فِئَتَيْنِ, the meaning being "why are you divided over the affairs of the hypocrites?", the muḍāf having been omitted. Second: that it is a ḥāl from فِئَتَيْنِ, i.e. "two parties divided over the hypocrites"; when it was placed before it, it was put in the accusative as a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:89-89.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَدُّوا لَوْ تَكْفُرُونَ كَمَا كَفَرُوا فَتَكُونُونَ سَوَاءً فَلَا تَتَّخِذُوا مِنْهُمْ أَوْلِيَاءَ حَتَّى يُهَاجِرُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَخُذُوهُمْ وَاقْتُلُوهُمْ حَيْثُ وَجَدْتُمُوهُمْ وَلَا تَتَّخِذُوا مِنْهُمْ وَلِيًّا وَلَا نَصِيرًا) (٨٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَمَا كَفَرُوا): the kāf is an adjective (naʿt) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and مَا is maṣdarī. (فَتَكُونُونَ): conjoined to تَكْفُرُونَ. And (سَوَاءً): with the meaning of مُسْتَوِينَ ("equal"); it is a maṣdar standing in the place of the active participle.

ukberi-tibyan:90-90.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ إِلَى قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِيثَاقٌ أَوْ جَاءُوكُمْ حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُمْ أَنْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ أَوْ يُقَاتِلُوا قَوْمَهُمْ وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَسَلَّطَهُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ فَلَقَاتَلُوكُمْ فَإِنِ اعْتَزَلُوكُمْ فَلَمْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ وَأَلْقَوْا إِلَيْكُمُ السَّلَمَ فَمَا جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ سَبِيلًا) (٩٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ): in the position of the accusative as an exception from the object pronoun in فَاقْتُلُوهُمْ. (بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِيثَاقٌ): you may make «مِيثَاقٌ» nominative by the adverbial phrase, since it has occurred as an adjective, or make it nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is in the position of the genitive. (حَصِرَتْ): there are two views about it.
First: this clause has no grammatical position; it is an imprecation against them, that their breasts be too constricted for fighting. Second: it has a position, and in this there are two views. First: it is genitive, as an adjective of قَوْمٍ, and what lies between them is also an adjective, while جَاءُوكُمْ is parenthetical. One of the Companions read: «بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِيثَاقٌ حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُمْ», omitting أَوْ جَاءُوكُمْ. Second: its position is accusative, and in this there are two views. First: its position is that of a ḥāl (circumstantial), with قَدْ intended, the implied wording being أَوْ جَاءُوكُمْ قَدْ حَصِرَتْ. Second: it is an adjective of an omitted qualified noun, i.e. جَاءُوكُمْ قَوْمًا حَصِرَتْ ("they came to you as a people whose breasts were constricted"), the omitted word being a preparatory ḥāl (ḥāl mūṭiʾa). It is also read (حَصِرَةً), in the accusative as a ḥāl, and in the genitive as an adjective of قَوْمٍ. And if حَصِرَةٌ has been read in the nominative, then it is a khabar (predicate) with صُدُورُهُمْ as mubtadaʾ, and the clause is a ḥāl. (أَنْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ): i.e. عَنْ أَنْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ ("from fighting you"); so it is in the position of the accusative or the genitive, according to the disagreement we have mentioned. (لَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ سَبِيلًا): لَكُمْ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to جَعَلَ, and عَلَيْهِمْ is a ḥāl from السَّبِيل, because the implied wording is سَبِيلًا كَائِنًا عَلَيْهِمْ ("a way existing against them").

ukberi-tibyan:91-91.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَتَجِدُونَ آخَرِينَ يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَأْمَنُوكُمْ وَيَأْمَنُوا قَوْمَهُمْ كُلَّمَا رُدُّوا إِلَى الْفِتْنَةِ أُرْكِسُوا فِيهَا.) (٩١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أُرْكِسُوا): the majority read it with the hamza retained; it is transitive to a single object.
It has also been read «رُكِّسُوا», the doubling being for both weight and intensification (al-takthīr). There is another dialectal form in it, namely رَكَسَهُ اللَّهُ, without hamza and without doubling, but I do not know of anyone who read it so.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أُمَّهَاتُكُمْ وَبَنَاتُكُمْ وَأَخَوَاتُكُمْ وَعَمَّاتُكُمْ وَخَالَاتُكُمْ وَبَنَاتُ الْأَخِ وَبَنَاتُ الْأُخْتِ وَأُمَّهَاتُكُمُ اللَّاتِي أَرْضَعْنَكُمْ وَأَخَوَاتُكُمْ مِنَ الرَّضَاعَةِ وَأُمَّهَاتُ نِسَائِكُمْ وَرَبَائِبُكُمُ اللَّاتِي فِي حُجُورِكُمْ مِنْ نِسَائِكُمُ اللَّاتِي دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ فَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُونُوا دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَحَلَائِلُ أَبْنَائِكُمُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ أَصْلَابِكُمْ وَأَنْ تَجْمَعُوا بَيْنَ الْأُخْتَيْنِ إِلَّا مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا) (٢٣).
His saying: (أُمَّهَاتُكُمْ): the hāʾ is redundant (zāʾida). This occurs only with rational beings; for non-rational beings one says أُمَّاتُ الْبَهَائِمِ ("the mothers of the beasts"). Each of the two forms has occurred, rarely, where the other belongs, so one says أُمَّاتُ الرِّجَالِ and أُمَّهَاتُ الْبَهَائِمِ. (وَبَنَاتُكُمْ): the final radical (lām) of the word is omitted, and its pattern is فَعَاتُكُمْ; the omitted letter is a wāw or a yāʾ, and we have mentioned it.
As for بِنْتٌ, the tāʾ in it is a substitute for the omitted lām, not the tāʾ of the feminine, because the letter before the feminine tāʾ is not vowelless, and the feminine tāʾ turns into hāʾ in pause. So بَنَاتٌ is not the plural of بِنْتٌ but of بَنَةٌ; the bāʾ was given kasra [in بِنْت] to signal the omitted letter. This is according to al-Farrāʾ. Others said: its basic vowel is fatḥa, and on that basis its plural and its masculine came, namely بَنُونَ; this is the school of the Basrans. As for أُخْتٌ, the tāʾ in it is a substitute for the wāw, because it is from الْأُخُوَّة ("brotherhood"); its plural is أَخَوَاتٌ.
If it is asked: why was the omitted letter restored in أَخَوَات but not restored in بَنَات? It is answered: each of the two plurals was modelled on its masculine. In the masculine of بَنَات the omitted letter was not restored; rather it came defective in the plural, and they said بَنُونَ; whereas in the plural of أَخٌ they said إِخْوَةٌ and إِخْوَانٌ, so the omitted letter was restored. الْعَمَّةُ is the feminine of الْعَمُّ (paternal uncle), and الْخَالَةُ is the feminine of الْخَالُ (maternal uncle); its alif is converted from a wāw, because you say in the plural أَخْوَالٌ. (مِنَ الرَّضَاعَةِ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from أَخَوَاتُكُمْ, i.e. "and forbidden to you are your sisters, being from suckling". (اللَّاتِي دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ): a naʿt (adjective) of the نِسَائِكُمْ that immediately precedes it; it is not an adjective of the نِسَائِكُمْ in his saying «وَأُمَّهَاتُ نِسَائِكُمْ», for two reasons. First: the first نِسَائِكُمْ is genitive by the genitive construct, and the second نِسَائِكُمْ is genitive by مِنْ, so the two genitives differ, and an adjective is not applied to what is of this kind, just as when the governing differs. Second: the mother of a woman becomes forbidden by the mere marriage contract according to the majority, whereas her daughter becomes forbidden only by consummation, so the meaning differs. (وَمِنْ نِسَائِكُمُ): [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has مِنْ نِسَائِكُمُ without wāw.] in the position of a ḥāl from رَبَائِبُكُمْ, or, if you wish, from the pronoun in the preposition phrase that is the ṣila (relative clause); its implied form being "who are settled in your care, being from your women". (وَأَنْ تَجْمَعُوا): in the nominative position, conjoined to أُمَّهَاتُكُمْ. And (إِلَّا مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ): a disjoined (munqaṭiʿ) exception, in the accusative position.

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالْمُحْصَنَاتُ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ كِتَابَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأُحِلَّ لَكُمْ مَا وَرَاءَ ذَلِكُمْ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا بِأَمْوَالِكُمْ مُحْصِنِينَ غَيْرَ مُسَافِحِينَ فَمَا اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِهِ مِنْهُنَّ فَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا تَرَاضَيْتُمْ بِهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ الْفَرِيضَةِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا) (٢٤).
His saying: (وَالْمُحْصَنَاتُ): it is conjoined to «أُمَّهَاتُكُمْ», and «مِنَ النِّسَاءِ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it.
The majority read the ṣād with fatḥa here, because what is meant by them is married women, and a married woman is مُحْصَنَة with fatḥa, because her husband has made her chaste (أَحْصَنَهَا), i.e. kept her virtuous. As for الْمُحْصَنَات elsewhere than this place, it is read with fatḥa and with kasra, and both are well known: the kasra on the basis that the women guarded their private parts, or their husbands; and the fatḥa on the basis that they were made chaste by husbands or by Islam. The derivation of the word is from al-taḥṣīn, which is "protecting, preventing".
(إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتْ): a joined (muttaṣil) exception, in the accusative position. The meaning is: "Forbidden to you are married women, except captives, for they are lawful even if they have husbands." (كِتَابَ اللَّهِ): it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) by an omitted كَتَبَ, indicated by his saying «حُرِّمَتْ», because the prohibition was written (prescribed). It is also said: it is accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "hold fast to the Book of Allah". And (عَلَيْكُمْ): incitement (ighrāʾ).
The Kufans said: it [عَلَيْكُمْ] is an incitement, and the object [كِتَابَ اللَّهِ] has been placed before it. In our view this is not permissible, because عَلَيْكُمْ and its like are weak governors and have no freedom to have their object placed before them. And «كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمْ» was also read, i.e. Allah prescribed that for you. On the first view, عَلَيْكُمْ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb that puts the maṣdar in the accusative, not to the maṣdar, because the maṣdar here is a supplement (faḍla). It is also said: it is attached to the maṣdar itself, because it stands in for the verb, since the verb is not mentioned with it; so it is like your saying مُرُورًا بِزَيْدٍ, i.e. "pass by (Zayd)". (وَأُحِلَّ لَكُمْ): read with fatḥa, with the agent named, conjoined to the verb that puts كِتَاب in the accusative; and with ḍamma, conjoined to حُرِّمَتْ. (مَا وَرَاءَ ذَلِكُمْ): there are two views on مَا.
First: it means مَنْ ("whoever"); on this view his saying «أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا» is in a genitive or accusative position, on the implied form "by (بِأَنْ) seeking" or "in order (لِأَنْ) to seek", i.e. "permitted to you are women other than those we have mentioned, through dowries". Second: «مَا» means الَّذِي ("that which"), and الَّذِي stands for the act, i.e. "and permitted to you is obtaining what lies beyond that forbidden act", and أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا is a badal (substitute) from it; and on this view أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا may also be as it was in the first view. And (مُحْصِنِينَ): a ḥāl from the agent in تَبْتَغُوا. (فَمَا اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ): there are two views on «مَا». First: it means مَنْ, and the hāʾ in «بِهِ» refers back to its wording. Second: it means الَّذِي, and the khabar (predicate) is «فَآتُوهُنَّ», with the pronoun referring back from it omitted, i.e. "for its sake". On the first view it may be conditional, its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) being فَآتُوهُنَّ, and the khabar is the protasis together with its apodosis, or the apodosis alone, according to what we have mentioned in more than one place. On the first view it may also mean الَّذِي and not be conditional, but rather in the nominative position as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ as its ṣila (relative clause) and the khabar فَآتُوهُنَّ. [Translator's note: so in the source ("on the first view"); the context suggests the second view may be meant in one of these two places.]
It may not be maṣdariyya, because of the corruption of meaning, and because the hāʾ in «بِهِ» refers back to مَا, and no pronoun refers back to maṣdariyya مَا. (مِنْهُنَّ): a ḥāl from the hāʾ in بِهِ. (فَرِيضَةً): a maṣdar of an omitted verb, or in the position of a ḥāl, according to what we mentioned in the verse of the bequest.

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنْكُمْ طَوْلًا أَنْ يَنْكِحَ الْمُحْصَنَاتِ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ فَمِنْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ مِنْ فَتَيَاتِكُمُ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِإِيمَانِكُمْ بَعْضُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ فَانْكِحُوهُنَّ بِإِذْنِ أَهْلِهِنَّ وَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ مُحْصَنَاتٍ غَيْرَ مُسَافِحَاتٍ وَلَا مُتَّخِذَاتِ أَخْدَانٍ فَإِذَا أُحْصِنَّ فَإِنْ أَتَيْنَ بِفَاحِشَةٍ فَعَلَيْهِنَّ نِصْفُ مَا عَلَى الْمُحْصَنَاتِ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ الْعَنَتَ مِنْكُمْ وَأَنْ تَصْبِرُوا خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) (٢٥).
His saying: (وَمَنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ): a conditional, and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is «فَمِمَّا مَلَكَتْ». And (مِنْكُمْ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يَسْتَطِعْ. (طَوْلًا): the object of يَسْتَطِعْ. It is also said: it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "for lack of means (الطَّوْل)". As for «أَنْ يَنْكِحَ», there are two views. First: it is a badal (substitute) from طَوْل, and it is the substitution of a thing for the same thing, both referring to one thing, because الطَّوْل is ability, or surplus means, and marriage is power and means. Second: that it is not a badal but is governed by طَوْل, and on this there are two views. One: it is accusative by طَوْل, because the implied form is "and whoever is unable to attain marriage with the chaste women"; it is from your saying طُلْتُهُ, i.e. "I attained it". From this is the saying of al-Farazdaq:
إِنَّ الْفَرَزْدَقَ صَخْرَةٌ عَادِيَّةٌ ... طَالَتْ فَلَيْسَ يَنَالُهَا الْأَوْعَالَا
("Al-Farazdaq is an ancient rock that has risen high beyond the mountain goats, so they cannot reach it.")
i.e. "it rose above (طَالَتْ) the mountain goats". The other: that it is on the implied omission of a preposition, i.e. "to (إِلَى) marry", the implied form being "and whoever cannot find a means of access to marrying the chaste women".
It is also said: the omitted element is the lām; on this view it is in the position of an adjective of طَوْل, and الطَّوْل is the dowry, i.e. "a dowry serving for him to marry".
It is also said: with the lām implied, it is the object of الطَّوْل, i.e. "means for the sake of marrying them".
(فَمِنْ مَا): there are two views on «مِنْ». First: it is redundant (zāʾida), the implied form being "then let him marry what [your right hands] possess".
Second: it is not redundant, and the implied verb is omitted, its implied form being "then let him marry a woman from what [your right hands] possess", and on this view «مِنْ» is an adjective of the omitted noun. It is also said: the object of the omitted verb is «فَتَيَاتِكُمْ», and the second مِنْ is redundant. And (الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ), on these views, is an adjective of الْفَتَيَات. It is also said: the object of the omitted verb is «الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ», the implied form being "from your maidens, the believing maidens". The position of «مِنْ فَتَيَاتِكُمْ», when «مِنْ» is not redundant, is a ḥāl from the omitted hāʾ in مَلَكَتْ. It is also said: there is a fronting and postponing in the phrase, its implied form being "then let some of you marry some of the maidens"; on this view his saying «وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِإِيمَانِكُمْ» is parenthetical between the verb and the agent, and (بَعْضُكُمْ) is the fāʿil (agent) of the omitted verb. The good view is that بَعْضُكُمْ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «مِنْ بَعْضٍ» its khabar (predicate), i.e. "you are of one kind with one another in lineage and religion", so the free man should not hold himself above the slave woman when there is need. It is also said: (فَمِمَّا مَلَكَتْ) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then the one to be married is from what [your right hands] possess". (مُحْصَنَاتٍ): a ḥāl from the object in «وَآتُوهُنَّ». (وَلَا مُتَّخِذَاتِ): conjoined to مُحْصَنَات, and the genitive construct is not a pure (true) one. الْأَخْدَان is the plural of خِدْنٌ ("secret lover"), like عِدْلٌ and أَعْدَالٌ. (فَإِذَا أُحْصِنَّ): read with ḍamma on the hamza, i.e. by husbands; and with fatḥa on it, i.e. they guarded their private parts. (فَإِنْ أَتَيْنَ): the fāʾ is the answer of إِذَا. (فَعَلَيْهِنَّ): the apodosis of إِنْ. (مِنَ الْعَذَابِ): in the position of a ḥāl from the pronoun in the preposition phrase, and what governs it is what governs its owner. It may not be a ḥāl from مَا, because مَا is genitive by the genitive construct and so has no governor [able to govern a ḥāl]. (ذَلِكَ): a mubtadaʾ. (لِمَنْ خَشِيَ): the khabar, i.e. "permissible for one who fears fornication". (وَأَنْ تَصْبِرُوا): a mubtadaʾ, and (خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ) is its khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:92-92.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ أَنْ يَقْتُلَ مُؤْمِنًا إِلَّا خَطَأً وَمَنْ قَتَلَ مُؤْمِنًا خَطَأً فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ وَدِيَةٌ مُسَلَّمَةٌ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَصَّدَّقُوا فَإِنْ كَانَ مِنْ قَوْمٍ عَدُوٍّ لَكُمْ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ وَإِنْ كَانَ مِنْ قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِيثَاقٌ فَدِيَةٌ مُسَلَّمَةٌ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ وَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ تَوْبَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا) (٩٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ أَنْ يَقْتُلَ مُؤْمِنًا): أَنْ يَقْتُلَ is in the position of the nominative as the noun (ism) of كَانَ, and لِمُؤْمِنٍ is its khabar (predicate). (إِلَّا خَطَأً): an exception not from the same kind as the first (i.e. disjoined), because error does not fall under legal obligation; the meaning is: "but if he kills by mistake, then the ruling on him is such-and-such". (فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ): فَتَحْرِيرُ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar is omitted, i.e. فَعَلَيْهِ تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ ("then upon him is the freeing of a slave"). It may also be a khabar with the mubtadaʾ omitted, i.e. فَالْوَاجِبُ عَلَيْهِ تَحْرِيرٌ ("then what is obligatory upon him is freeing"); and the clause is the khabar of مَنْ. «خَطَأً» has also been read without hamza, and there are two views about it. First: that he lightened the hamza and changed it into an alif, so it became like a maqṣūr noun. Second: that he dropped it outright, so it remained like دَامٍ. In وَمَنْ قَتَلَ مُؤْمِنًا خَطَأً, it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. قَتْلًا خَطَأً ("a mistaken killing"); and it may be a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. مُخْطِئًا ("erring"). The original form of دِيَةٍ is وَدْيَةٌ, like عِدَةٍ and زِنَةٍ; this maṣdar is a name for the thing paid, like الْهِبَة in the sense of "the thing given"; that is why He said (مُسَلَّمَةٌ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ) "handed over to his family", for an act is not handed over. [Translator's note: the analogy with عِدَةٍ and زِنَةٍ points to the vocalization وِدْيَةٌ (with kasra on the wāw); the printed text has fatḥa.] (إِلَّا أَنْ يَصَّدَّقُوا): it is said that it is a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); and it is said that it is joined (muttaṣil), the meaning being: "then upon him is blood-money in every circumstance, except in the circumstance of its being given up to him as charity".
(فَإِنْ كَانَ): i.e. the one killed; «مِنْ قَوْمٍ» is the khabar of كَانَ. And «لَكُمْ» is an adjective of عَدُوٍّ. It is also said: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it, because عَدُوٌّ has the meaning of مُعَادٍ ("hostile"), and the pattern faʿūl operates as fāʿil (the active participle) does.
فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ, i.e. "then upon the killer". (فَصِيَامُ): i.e. فَعَلَيْهِ صِيَامُ ("then upon him is fasting"); outside the Quran the accusative would be permissible, on the implied wording فَلْيَصُمْ شَهْرَيْنِ ("let him fast two months"). (تَوْبَةً): a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the implied wording is: "He prescribed that for you as a repentance from Him". It is not permissible for what governs it to be صَوْمٌ ("fasting") except on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being "for the occurrence of repentance" or "for the attainment of repentance from Allah". It is also said: it is a maṣdar in the accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being تَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ تَوْبَةً مِنْهُ ("He turned to you in repentance from Him"). It is not permissible for it to be in the position of a ḥāl, because if you said "then upon him is the fasting of two months, repenting from Allah", it would not be permissible; but if you assume the omission of a muḍāf it is permissible, i.e. "possessor of repentance from Allah". And (مِنَ اللَّهِ): an adjective of «تَوْبَةً». Outside the Quran تَوْبَةٌ in the nominative would be permissible, i.e. ذَلِكَ تَوْبَةٌ ("that is a repentance").

ukberi-tibyan:93-93.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَنْ يَقْتُلْ مُؤْمِنًا مُتَعَمِّدًا فَجَزَاؤُهُ جَهَنَّمُ خَالِدًا فِيهَا وَغَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَلَعَنَهُ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُ عَذَابًا عَظِيمًا) (٩٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَنْ يَقْتُلْ): مَنْ is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «مُتَعَمِّدًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of the killer; «فَجَزَاؤُهُ» is a mubtadaʾ and «جَهَنَّمُ» its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of مَنْ. And (خَالِدًا): a ḥāl from something omitted, its implied form being يُجَازِهَا خَالِدًا فِيهَا ("he is requited with it, abiding in it"); if you wish you may make it from the nominative pronoun, and if you wish from the accusative one. It is also said: the implied wording is جَازَاهُ ("He requited him"), as shown by His saying «وَغَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَلَعَنَهُ», where He conjoined the past verb to it; on this view «خَالِدًا» is a ḥāl from the accusative pronoun and nothing else. It is not permissible for it to be a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «جَزَاؤُهُ», for two reasons. First: that it would be a ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi. Second: that the khabar of the mubtadaʾ would separate the one to whom the ḥāl refers from the ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:94-94.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَتَبَيَّنُوا وَلَا تَقُولُوا لِمَنْ أَلْقَى إِلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامَ لَسْتَ مُؤْمِنًا تَبْتَغُونَ عَرَضَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا فَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ مَغَانِمُ كَثِيرَةٌ كَذَلِكَ كُنْتُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَمَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ فَتَبَيَّنُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا) (٩٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَتَبَيَّنُوا): it is read with bāʾ, yāʾ and nūn, from al-tabyīn ("making clear"), and with thāʾ, bāʾ and tāʾ (فَتَثَبَّتُوا), from al-tathabbut ("verifying"); the two are close in meaning. (لِمَنْ أَلْقَى): مَنْ has the meaning of الَّذِي, or is an indefinite qualified noun (nakira mawṣūfa); and أَلْقَى has the meaning of يُلْقِي, because a prohibition is valid only regarding the future. The man concerning whom the verse was revealed said to someone who offered him the greeting of peace, "You are not a believer", and killed him. And (السَّلَامَ): with the alif, it is the greeting; it is also read with fatḥa on the lām without alif (السَّلَمَ), and with the lām quiescent, with kasra on the sīn and with fatḥa (السِّلْمَ / السَّلْمَ), and that means surrender and peace-making. (لَسْتَ مُؤْمِنًا): in the position of the accusative by the verb of saying. The majority read with ḍamma on the first mīm and kasra on the second (مُؤْمِنًا), and it is derived from al-īmān ("faith"). It is also read with fatḥa on the second mīm (مُؤْمَنًا), which is the passive participle from أَمِنْتُهُ ("I gave him security"). (تَبْتَغُونَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in يَقُولُوا. (كَذَلِكَ): the kāf is the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ, and it has been placed before it and before its noun. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ): the majority read إِنَّ with kasra, as a resumptive clause; it has also been read with fatḥa (أَنَّ), in which case it is governed by تَبَيَّنُوا.

ukberi-tibyan:95-95.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا يَسْتَوِي الْقَاعِدُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ وَالْمُجَاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ الْمُجَاهِدِينَ بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ عَلَى الْقَاعِدِينَ دَرَجَةً وَكُلًّا وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْحُسْنَى وَفَضَّلَ اللَّهُ الْمُجَاهِدِينَ عَلَى الْقَاعِدِينَ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا) (٩٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); the one to whom the ḥāl refers is «الْقَاعِدُونَ», and what governs it is «يَسْتَوِي». It may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in الْقَاعِدِينَ, in which case what governs it is الْقَاعِدُونَ, because the alif and lām have the meaning of الَّذِي. (غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ): in the nominative as an adjective of «الْقَاعِدُونَ», because no specific group of people is intended by it. It is also said: it is a badal (substitute) from الْقَاعِدِينَ. It is also read in the accusative, as an exception from الْقَاعِدِينَ or from الْمُؤْمِنِينَ, or as a ḥāl; and in the genitive as an adjective of الْمُؤْمِنِينَ. (وَالْمُجَاهِدُونَ): conjoined to الْقَاعِدِينَ. (بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to الْمُجَاهِدِينَ. (دَرَجَةً): it is said that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of تَفْضِيلًا ("a preferring"). It is also said: a ḥāl, i.e. ذَوِي دَرَجَةٍ ("possessing a degree"). It is also said: it is on the assumption of the omission of the preposition, i.e. بِدَرَجَةٍ ("by a degree"). It is also said: it occupies the place of an adverbial, i.e. "in a degree and rank".
(وَكُلًّا): the first object of «وَعَدَ», and «الْحُسْنَى» is the second. It has also been read وَكُلٌّ, i.e. وَكُلُّهُمْ ("and all of them"), with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. وَعَدَهُ اللَّهُ ("Allah promised it"). «أَجْرًا»: it is said that it is a maṣdar from other than the verb's own root, because the meaning of "He preferred them" is "He rewarded them".
It is also said: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because "He preferred them" means "He gave them". It is also said: the implied wording is بِأَجْرٍ ("with a reward").

ukberi-tibyan:96-96.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (دَرَجَاتٍ مِنْهُ وَمَغْفِرَةً وَرَحْمَةً وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا) (٩٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (دَرَجَاتٍ): it is said that it is a badal (substitute) from أَجْرًا. It is also said: the implied wording is ذَوِي دَرَجَاتٍ ("possessing degrees"). It is also said: فِي دَرَجَاتٍ ("in degrees"). (وَمَغْفِرَةً): it is said that it is conjoined to what precedes it. It is also said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. وَغَفَرَ لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةً ("and He forgave them with forgiveness"). And (رَحْمَةً): likewise.

ukberi-tibyan:97-97.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ ظَالِمِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ قَالُوا فِيمَ كُنْتُمْ قَالُوا كُنَّا مُسْتَضْعَفِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ قَالُوا أَلَمْ تَكُنْ أَرْضُ اللَّهِ وَاسِعَةً فَتُهَاجِرُوا فِيهَا فَأُولَئِكَ مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَسَاءَتْ مَصِيرًا) (٩٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تَوَفَّاهُمُ): the original is تَتَوَفَّاهُمْ; it may also be a past verb. It is also read with imāla (inclination of the vowel).
(ظَالِمِي): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in تَتَوَفَّاهُمْ; the annexation is not pure (ghayr maḥḍa), i.e. ظَالِمِينَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ ("wronging themselves"). (قَالُوا): there are two views about it. First: it is a ḥāl from الْمَلَائِكَة, with «قَدْ» implied with it, and the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ is «فَأُولَئِكَ»; the fāʾ entered because of the vagueness in الَّذِي resembling a condition, and إِنَّ does not prevent this because it does not change the meaning of the nominal sentence. Second: that قَالُوا is the khabar of إِنَّ, with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. قَالُوا لَهُمْ ("they said to them"). (فِيمَ كُنْتُمْ): the alif of interrogative «مَا» was dropped together with the preposition for the reason we mentioned at His saying (فَلِمَ تَقْتُلُونَ أَنْبِيَاءَ اللَّهِ); the preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar of كُنْتُمْ. And (فِي الْأَرْضِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to مُسْتَضْعَفِينَ. (أَلَمْ تَكُنْ): an interrogative meaning rebuke. (فَتُهَاجِرُوا): accusative as the answer to the interrogative, because the negation has become an affirmation through the interrogative. (وَسَاءَتْ): it has the status of بِئْسَتْ ("how evil").

ukberi-tibyan:98-98.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِلَّا الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ وَالنِّسَاءِ وَالْوِلْدَانِ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ حِيلَةً وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ سَبِيلًا) (٩٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ): an exception not from the same kind as the first, because the first is His saying «تَتَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ ظَالِمِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ», to which the pronoun of مَأْوَاهُمْ refers; these were sinners for staying behind from the emigration despite being able, while إِلَّا الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ are those who were incapable; hence it is disjoined (munqaṭiʿ). And (مِنَ الرِّجَالِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ, or from الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ itself. (لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ): it may be resumptive, and it may be a ḥāl explaining the meaning of being oppressed.

ukberi-tibyan:100-100.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَنْ يُهَاجِرْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ يَجِدْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مُرَاغَمًا كَثِيرًا وَسَعَةً وَمَنْ يَخْرُجْ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ مُهَاجِرًا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ يُدْرِكْهُ الْمَوْتُ فَقَدْ وَقَعَ أَجْرُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا) (١٠٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُهَاجِرًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يَخْرُجُ. (ثُمَّ يُدْرِكْهُ): jussive (majzūm), conjoined to يَخْرُجُ. It is also read in the nominative as resumptive, i.e. ثُمَّ هُوَ يُدْرِكُهُ ("then it overtakes him"). It has also been read in the accusative on the assumption of an implied أَنْ, because it was not conjoined to the protasis in form, so it was conjoined to it in meaning, as occurs with the wāw and the fāʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:101-101.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَقْصُرُوا مِنَ الصَّلَاةِ إِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَنْ يَفْتِنَكُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنَّ الْكَافِرِينَ كَانُوا لَكُمْ عَدُوًّا مُبِينًا) (١٠١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ تَقْصُرُوا): i.e. فِي أَنْ تَقْصُرُوا ("in shortening"); parallels of it have preceded. And (مِنْ): redundant (zāʾida) according to al-Akhfash; according to Sībawayh it is an adjective of something omitted, i.e. شَيْئًا مِنَ الصَّلَاةِ ("something of the prayer"). [Translator's note: the printed text reads شُئِيَا, evidently a misprint for شَيْئًا.] (عَدُوًّا): in the place of أَعْدَاءٍ ("enemies"). It is also said: عَدُوٌّ is a maṣdar (verbal noun) on the pattern faʿūl, like الْقَبُول and الْوَلُوع; that is why it was not made plural. And (لَكُمْ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from عَدُوٍّ, or attached (mutaʿalliq) to كَانَ.

ukberi-tibyan:102-102.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا كُنْتَ فِيهِمْ فَأَقَمْتَ لَهُمُ الصَّلَاةَ فَلْتَقُمْ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْهُمْ مَعَكَ وَلْيَأْخُذُوا أَسْلِحَتَهُمْ فَإِذَا سَجَدُوا فَلْيَكُونُوا مِنْ وَرَائِكُمْ وَلْتَأْتِ طَائِفَةٌ أُخْرَى لَمْ يُصَلُّوا فَلْيُصَلُّوا مَعَكَ وَلْيَأْخُذُوا حِذْرَهُمْ وَأَسْلِحَتَهُمْ وَدَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْ تَغْفُلُونَ عَنْ أَسْلِحَتِكُمْ وَأَمْتِعَتِكُمْ فَيَمِيلُونَ عَلَيْكُمْ مَيْلَةً وَاحِدَةً وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِنْ كَانَ بِكُمْ أَذًى مِنْ مَطَرٍ أَوْ كُنْتُمْ مَرْضَى أَنْ تَضَعُوا أَسْلِحَتَكُمْ وَخُذُوا حِذْرَكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ أَعَدَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابًا مُهِينًا) (١٠٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَمْ يُصَلُّوا): in the position of the nominative as an adjective of طَائِفَةٌ; the pronoun came according to the meaning of الطَّائِفَة ("the party"); had He said لَمْ تُصَلِّ, it would have been according to its wording. And (لَوْ تَغْفُلُونَ): with the meaning of أَنْ تَغْفُلُوا ("that you be heedless"). And (أَنْ تَضَعُوا): i.e. فِي أَنْ تَضَعُوا ("in laying down").

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَيَهْدِيَكُمْ سُنَنَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَيَتُوبَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ) (٢٦).
His saying: (يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ): the object of يُرِيدُ is omitted, its implied form being "Allah wills that", i.e. the forbidding of what He has forbidden and the permitting of what He has permitted, in order to make clear. The lām in لِيُبَيِّنَ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يُرِيدُ. It is also said: the lām is redundant (zāʾida), and the implied form is "Allah wills to (أَنْ) make clear", so the accusative is by أَنْ.

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَيُرِيدُ الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ الشَّهَوَاتِ أَنْ تَمِيلُوا مَيْلًا عَظِيمًا) (٢٧).
His saying: (وَيُرِيدُ الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ الشَّهَوَاتِ): conjoined to his saying وَاللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْكُمْ, except that He began the first clause with the noun and the second with the verb. It may not be read with the accusative [i.e. وَيُرِيدَ], because the meaning would become "and Allah wills to turn to you, and wills that those who follow desires should will", and that is not the meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُخَفِّفَ عَنْكُمْ وَخُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ ضَعِيفًا) (٢٨).
His saying: (وَخُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ ضَعِيفًا): ضَعِيفًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is also said: a tamyīz (specification), because it can be interpreted with مِنْ; but this is nothing. It is also said: the implied form is "and man was created from something weak", i.e. from clay, or from a drop, a clinging clot and a lump of flesh, as He said: (اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ ضَعْفٍ); so when the preposition and the qualified noun were omitted, the adjective became accusative by the verb itself.

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِالْبَاطِلِ إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ تِجَارَةً عَنْ تَرَاضٍ مِنْكُمْ وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُمْ رَحِيمًا) (٢٩).
His saying: (إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ تِجَارَةً): the exception is disjoined (munqaṭiʿ), not of the kind of the first. It is also said: it is joined (muttaṣil), the implied form being "do not consume it by any means except that it be trade"; this is weak, because He said بِالْبَاطِلِ ("wrongfully"), and trade is not of the kind of what is wrongful.
There is an omitted muḍāf in the phrase, i.e. "except in the state of its being trade" or "at the time of its being trade". تِجَارَةٌ in the nominative is on the basis that kāna is complete (tāmma), and in the accusative on the basis that it is the incomplete (nāqiṣa) one, the implied form being "except that the dealing, or the trading, be trade". It is also said: its implied form is "except that the wealth be trade". (عَنْ تَرَاضٍ): in the position of an adjective of «تِجَارَةً». (مِنْكُمْ): an adjective of تَرَاضٍ.

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ عُدْوَانًا وَظُلْمًا فَسَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِ نَارًا وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرًا) (٣٠).
His saying: (وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ): «مَنْ» is in the nominative position as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is (فَسَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِ).
(عُدْوَانًا وَظُلْمًا): two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose). The majority read the nūn of نُصْلِيهِ with ḍamma, and it is read with fatḥa; these are two dialectal usages: one says أَصْلَيْتُهُ النَّارَ and صَلَيْتُهُ ("I made him roast in the fire").

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنْ تَجْتَنِبُوا كَبَائِرَ مَا تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ نُكَفِّرْ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ وَنُدْخِلْكُمْ مُدْخَلًا كَرِيمًا) (٣١).
His saying: (مُدْخَلًا): read with fatḥa on the mīm [مَدْخَلًا], and it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of دَخَلَ, the implied form being "and We shall admit him, and he will enter an entering (مَدْخَلًا)", i.e. an entry (دُخُولًا). When mafʿal occurs as a maṣdar it is the maṣdar of faʿala; as for afʿala, its maṣdar is mufʿal with ḍamma on the mīm, just as the hamza takes ḍamma [in the imperfect]. It is also said: مَدْخَل here, with fatḥa on the mīm, is a place, and so it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), like أَدْخَلْتُهُ بَيْتًا ("I made him enter a house").

ukberi-tibyan:32-32.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَتَمَنَّوْا مَا فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ بِهِ بَعْضَكُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ لِلرِّجَالِ نَصِيبٌ مِمَّا اكْتَسَبُوا وَلِلنِّسَاءِ نَصِيبٌ مِمَّا اكْتَسَبْنَ وَاسْأَلُوا اللَّهَ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمًا) (٣٢).
His saying: (مَا فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ): «مَا» means الَّذِي ("that which"), or is an indefinite qualified noun; the pronoun referring back is the hāʾ in «بِهِ», and the object is «بَعْضَكُمْ».
«وَاسْأَلُوا اللَّهَ» is read سَلُوا without hamza, and (وَاسْأَلُوا) with hamza; this was mentioned at his saying (سَلْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ). The object of اسْأَلُوا is omitted, i.e. "something", «مِنْ فَضْلِهِ» ("of His bounty").

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنَا مَوَالِيَ مِمَّا تَرَكَ الْوَالِدَانِ وَالْأَقْرَبُونَ وَالَّذِينَ عَقَدَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ فَآتُوهُمْ نَصِيبَهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدًا) (٣٣).
His saying: (وَلِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنَا): the muḍāf ilayhi is omitted, and there are two views on it. First: its implied form is "and for every person We have made heirs (مَوَالِيَ) who inherit from him". Second: "and for all wealth". The first object of جَعَلَ is «مَوَالِيَ», and the second is لِكُلٍّ; the implied form being "and We have made inheritors for every deceased person", or "for all wealth". (مِمَّا تَرَكَ): there are two views. First: it is an adjective of the omitted مَال, i.e. "of wealth that «الْوَالِدَانِ» left". Second: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb indicated by الْمَوَالِي, its implied form being "who inherit what [the parents] left". It is also said: «مَا» means مَنْ, i.e. "for every one of those whom the parents left". (وَالَّذِينَ عَقَدَتْ): there are three views on its position. First: it is conjoined to مَوَالِيَ, i.e. "and We have made those with whom [your oaths] made a pact inheritors"; this was the case and was then abrogated, so his saying «فَآتُوهُمْ نَصِيبَهُمْ» is a tawkīd (emphasis). Second: its position is accusative by an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned, i.e. "and give those with whom [your oaths] made a pact". Third: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «فَآتُوهُمْ» is the khabar (predicate). عَاقَدَتْ is read with alif, with the object omitted, i.e. عَاقَدَتْهُمْ ("made a pact with them"); and it is read without alif, and the object is also omitted, together with the pronoun referring back, its implied form being "your oaths contracted their alliance (حِلْفَهُمْ)". It is also said: the implied form is "the possessors of your oaths contracted their alliance", and the muḍāf was omitted, because those who contract the oath are the ones swearing, not the oaths themselves.

ukberi-tibyan:34-34.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الرِّجَالُ قَوَّامُونَ عَلَى النِّسَاءِ بِمَا فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ وَبِمَا أَنْفَقُوا مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ فَالصَّالِحَاتُ قَانِتَاتٌ حَافِظَاتٌ لِلْغَيْبِ بِمَا حَفِظَ اللَّهُ وَاللَّاتِي تَخَافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ فَعِظُوهُنَّ وَاهْجُرُوهُنَّ فِي الْمَضَاجِعِ وَاضْرِبُوهُنَّ فَإِنْ أَطَعْنَكُمْ فَلَا تَبْغُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ سَبِيلًا إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيًّا كَبِيرًا) (٣٤).
His saying: (قَوَّامُونَ عَلَى النِّسَاءِ): «عَلَى» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to قَوَّامُونَ. And (بِمَا) is also attached to it; since the two particles have two different meanings, it is permissible for both to be attached to one thing; so «عَلَى», on this view, has a meaning other than the meaning of the bāʾ. The bāʾ may also be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and so be attached to something omitted, its implied form being "deserving it by Allah's preferring them"; the owner of the ḥāl is the pronoun in قَوَّامُونَ, and مَا is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun). As for «مَا» in his saying «وَبِمَا أَنْفَقُوا», it may be maṣdariyya, so that مِنْ is attached to أَنْفَقُوا and there is no ellipsis in the phrase; and it may mean الَّذِي, with the pronoun referring back omitted, i.e. "and by what they spent (أَنْفَقُوهُ)"; on this view «مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ» is a ḥāl. (فَالصَّالِحَاتُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject); «قَانِتَاتٌ حَافِظَاتٌ» are two khabars (predicates) of it.
It was also read: «فَالصَّوَالِحُ قَوَانِتُ حَوَافِظُ»; this is a broken plural of multitude (jamʿ taksīr) indicating abundance, whereas the sound plural does not by its original coinage indicate abundance, though it has been used for it, as in His saying: (وَهُمْ فِي الْغُرُفَاتِ آمِنُونَ). (بِمَا حَفِظَ اللَّهُ): in «مَا» there are three views: meaning الَّذِي; an indefinite qualified noun, with the pronoun referring back omitted on both these views; and maṣdariyya. It was also read بِمَا حَفِظَ اللَّهَ, with the name of Allah in the accusative; on this reading مَا means الَّذِي or is indefinite, and the muḍāf is omitted, the implied form being "by that which kept the command of Allah" or "the religion of Allah". Some said it [مَا] is maṣdariyya, the implied form being حَفِظَهُنَّ اللَّهَ ("their keeping Allah"); this is an error, because if it were so the verb would be devoid of the agent pronoun, since the agent here is a feminine plural, and its pronoun is made overt, so it would have to be بِمَا حَفِظَهُنَّ اللَّهُ. [Translator's note: so in the printed text; the argument requires the verb with an overt feminine plural agent pronoun, i.e. بِمَا حَفِظْنَ اللَّهَ.] This view has been defended, with the agent in it taken as referring to the genus, which is singular masculine, so no pronoun appears for it. (وَاللَّاتِي تَخَافُونَ): like His saying (وَاللَّاتِي يَأْتِينَ الْفَاحِشَةَ) and like (وَاللَّذَانِ يَأْتِيَانِهَا), and both have been discussed. (وَاهْجُرُوهُنَّ فِي الْمَضَاجِعِ): there are two views on «فِي». First: it is an adverb (ẓarf) for the shunning, i.e. "shun them in the places of lying down", i.e. leave their beds without ceasing to speak to them. Second: it denotes cause, i.e. "and shun them because of the beds", as you say: "in this crime there is a punishment". (فَلَا تَبْغُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ): there are two views on «تَبْغُوا». First: it is from al-baghy, which is injustice; on this view it is intransitive, and (سَبِيلًا) on this view is accusative on the implied omission of the preposition, i.e. "by any way". Second: it is from your saying بَغَيْتُ الْأَمْرَ, i.e. "I sought it"; on this view it is transitive and «سَبِيلًا» is its object, and عَلَيْهِنَّ is from the description of the way, so it is a ḥāl because it precedes it.

ukberi-tibyan:103-103.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِذَا قَضَيْتُمُ الصَّلَاةَ فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ قِيَامًا وَقُعُودًا وَعَلَى جُنُوبِكُمْ فَإِذَا اطْمَأْنَنْتُمْ فَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ إِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ كَانَتْ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ كِتَابًا مَوْقُوتًا) (١٠٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قِيَامًا وَقُعُودًا وَعَلَى جُنُوبِكُمْ): all of them are aḥwāl (circumstantial expressions; sing. ḥāl).
(اطْمَأْنَنْتُمْ): the hamza is a radical; the pattern of the word is ifʿalalla, and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is الطُّمَأْنِينَة, on the pattern fuʿallīla. As for their saying طَامَنَ رَأْسَهُ ("he lowered his head"), that is another root. And (مَوْقُوتًا): a passive participle from وَقَتَ, without doubling.

ukberi-tibyan:104-104.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَهِنُوا فِي ابْتِغَاءِ الْقَوْمِ إِنْ تَكُونُوا تَأْلَمُونَ فَإِنَّهُمْ يَأْلَمُونَ كَمَا تَأْلَمُونَ وَتَرْجُونَ مِنَ اللَّهِ مَا لَا يَرْجُونَ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا) (١٠٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنْ تَكُونُوا تَأْلَمُونَ): the majority read إِنْ with kasra, and it is conditional. It has also been read «أَنْ تَكُونُوا» with fatḥa, i.e. لِأَنْ تَكُونُوا ("because you are"). It is also read «تِيلَمُونَ», with kasra on the tāʾ and the hamza changed into yāʾ; this is a dialectal form.

ukberi-tibyan:105-105.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ لِتَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ بِمَا أَرَاكَ اللَّهُ وَلَا تَكُنْ لِلْخَائِنِينَ خَصِيمًا) (١٠٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِالْحَقِّ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْكِتَاب; parallels of it have passed. (أَرَاكَ): the hamza here makes the verb transitive. The verb is from رَأَيْتَ الشَّيْءَ when you adopt something as your view, and it is from al-raʾy ("opinion"); it is transitive to one object, and after the hamza it becomes transitive to two objects, one of them the kāf and the other omitted, i.e. أَرَاكَهُ ("He showed it to you").
It is also said: the meaning is عَلَّمَكَ ("He taught you"), which is also transitive to two objects, while before the doubling it is transitive to one, as in His saying «لَا تَعْلَمُونَهُمْ». (خَصِيمًا): with the meaning of مُخَاصِمٍ ("disputant"); the lām keeps its proper meaning, i.e. "for the sake of the treacherous". It is also said: it has the meaning of عَنْ ("on behalf of").

ukberi-tibyan:108-108.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَسْتَخْفُونَ مِنَ النَّاسِ وَلَا يَسْتَخْفُونَ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَهُوَ مَعَهُمْ إِذْ يُبَيِّتُونَ مَا لَا يَرْضَى مِنَ الْقَوْلِ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطًا) (١٠٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَسْتَخْفُونَ): with the meaning of "they seek concealment"; it is resumptive, with no grammatical position. (إِذْ يُبَيِّتُونَ): an adverbial (ẓarf) for what governs مَعَهُمْ.

ukberi-tibyan:109-109.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَا أَنْتُمْ هَؤُلَاءِ جَادَلْتُمْ عَنْهُمْ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا فَمَنْ يُجَادِلُ اللَّهَ عَنْهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَمْ مَنْ يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَكِيلًا) (١٠٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَا أَنْتُمْ هَؤُلَاءِ جَادَلْتُمْ): we have discussed it at His saying (ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ هَؤُلَاءِ تَقْتُلُونَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ). (أَمْ مَنْ): أَمْ here is disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa).

ukberi-tibyan:110-110.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا أَوْ يَظْلِمْ نَفْسَهُ ثُمَّ يَسْتَغْفِرِ اللَّهَ يَجِدِ اللَّهَ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا) (١١٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَوْ يَظْلِمْ نَفْسَهُ): أَوْ is for detailing what was left vague; we have mentioned the like of it in more than one place.

ukberi-tibyan:112-112.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَنْ يَكْسِبْ خَطِيئَةً أَوْ إِثْمًا ثُمَّ يَرْمِ بِهِ بَرِيئًا فَقَدِ احْتَمَلَ بُهْتَانًا وَإِثْمًا مُبِينًا) (١١٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ثُمَّ يَرْمِ بِهِ بَرِيئًا): the hāʾ refers back to الْإِثْم ("the sin"), and its referring back to it is evidence that al-khaṭīʾa ("the offence") has the same status as al-ithm. It is also said: it refers back to one of the two things indicated by أَوْ. It is also said: it refers back to the earning indicated by His saying «وَمَنْ يَكْسِبُ». It is also said: it refers back to what is earned, which the verb indicates.

ukberi-tibyan:113-113.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ وَرَحْمَتُهُ لَهَمَّتْ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْهُمْ أَنْ يُضِلُّوكَ وَمَا يُضِلُّونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَضُرُّونَكَ مِنْ شَيْءٍ وَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَعَلَّمَكَ مَا لَمْ تَكُنْ تَعْلَمُ وَكَانَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ عَظِيمًا) (١١٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ): concerning the response of (لَوْلَا) there are two views. First: it is His saying «لَهَمَّتْ»; on this view, no intention to mislead him occurred on the part of the group referred to.
Second: that the response is omitted, its implied form being لَأَضَلُّوكَ ("they would have misled you"); then He began anew and said لَهَمَّتْ, i.e. "that [group] did indeed intend". Like the omission of the response here is its omission in His saying (وَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ تَوَّابٌ حَكِيمٌ). (وَمَا يَضُرُّونَكَ مِنْ شَيْءٍ): «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), and «شَيْءٍ» has the meaning of ضَرَرٍ ("harm"), so it is in the position of the maṣdar (verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:114-114.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا خَيْرَ فِي كَثِيرٍ مِنْ نَجْوَاهُمْ إِلَّا مَنْ أَمَرَ بِصَدَقَةٍ أَوْ مَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ إِصْلَاحٍ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ ابْتِغَاءَ مَرْضَاةِ اللَّهِ فَسَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا) (١١٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ نَجْوَاهُمْ): in the position of the genitive as an adjective of كَثِيرٍ.
Concerning النَّجْوَى there are two views. First: it is the confiding together (al-tanājī). On this view there are two views concerning His saying إِلَّا مَنْ أَمَرَ. First: it is a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) in the position of the accusative, because مَنْ is for persons and is not of the same kind as confiding. Second: that there is an omitted muḍāf in the phrase, its implied form being إِلَّا نَجْوَى مَنْ أَمَرَ ("except the confiding of one who enjoins"); on this view it may be in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from نَجْوَاهُمْ, or in the position of the accusative according to the basic rule of the chapter of exception, and it is joined (muttaṣil). The other view: that النَّجْوَى is the people who confide together; of this kind is His saying (وَإِذْ هُمْ نَجْوَى). On this view the exception is joined, so it too is in the position of the genitive or the accusative, as has preceded.
(بَيْنَ النَّاسِ): it may be an adverbial (ẓarf) for إِصْلَاحٍ, or an adjective of it, in which case it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted.
And (ابْتِغَاءَ): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the alif of «مَرْضَاةِ» is from a wāw. (فَسَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِ): with nūn and with yāʾ (يُؤْتِيهِ), and it is clear.

ukberi-tibyan:115-115.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَنْ يُشَاقِقِ الرَّسُولَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ الْهُدَى وَيَتَّبِعْ غَيْرَ سَبِيلِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ نُوَلِّهِ مَا تَوَلَّى وَنُصْلِهِ جَهَنَّمَ وَسَاءَتْ مَصِيرًا) (١١٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَنْ يُشَاقِقِ): pronouncing the qāf separately (without assimilation) is permissible only because the second one became quiescent through the jussive, and its vowel is incidental, due to the meeting of two quiescent letters. The hāʾ in His saying (وَنُصْلِهِ) is like the hāʾ in (يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ), and we have spoken about it.

ukberi-tibyan:116-116.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَمَنْ يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا) (١١٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يَغْفِرُ.

ukberi-tibyan:117-117.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنْ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلَّا إِنَاثًا وَإِنْ يَدْعُونَ إِلَّا شَيْطَانًا مَرِيدًا) (١١٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا إِنَاثًا): it is the plural of أُنْثَى ("female") on the pattern fiʿāl, and what is meant by it is everything that has no spirit in it, such as a rock, the sun and the like. It is also read أُنْثَى, in the singular, the singular indicating the plural. It is also read «أُنُثًا», like رُسُلٍ; it may be a singular adjective, like امْرَأَةٌ جُنُبٌ ("a woman in a state of major ritual impurity"), and it may be the plural of أَنِيثٍ, like قَلِيبٍ and قُلُبٍ; they have said جِدِيدُ أَنِيثٍ in this sense. [Translator's note: the printed جِدِيدُ أَنِيثٍ is presumably حَدِيدٌ أَنِيثٌ, "soft iron".] It is also read «أُنْثًا», whose singular is وَثَنٌ, which is the idol; its original form in the plural is وُثُنٌ, as in the singular, except that the wāw was changed into hamza when it took a permanent ḍamma; it is like أَسَدٍ and أُسُدٍ. [Translator's note: given the explanation from وَثَنٌ, the intended reading is presumably «أُثُنًا».] It is also read with the wāw, according to the original, as a plural (وُثُنًا); and it is read with the thāʾ quiescent, with both the hamza and the wāw (أُثْنًا / وُثْنًا). And (مَرِيدًا): faʿīl, from al-tamarrud ("rebelliousness").

ukberi-tibyan:118-118.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ وَقَالَ لَأَتَّخِذَنَّ مِنْ عِبَادِكَ نَصِيبًا مَفْرُوضًا) (١١٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ): it may be another adjective of شَيْطَانٍ, and it may be resumptive, as an imprecation. (وَقَالَ): it admits three views. First: that the wāw conjoins قَالَ to «لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ», the fāʿil (agent) of قَالَ being the pronoun of Satan. Second: that it is the wāw of the ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. وَقَدْ قَالَ ("having said"). Third: that the clause is resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:119-119.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَأُضِلَّنَّهُمْ وَلَأُمَنِّيَنَّهُمْ وَلَآمُرَنَّهُمْ فَلَيُبَتِّكُنَّ آذَانَ الْأَنْعَامِ وَلَآمُرَنَّهُمْ فَلَيُغَيِّرُنَّ خَلْقَ اللَّهِ وَمَنْ يَتَّخِذِ الشَّيْطَانَ وَلِيًّا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ فَقَدْ خَسِرَ خُسْرَانًا مُبِينًا) (١١٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَأُضِلَّنَّهُمْ): the object of these verbs is omitted, i.e. لَأُضِلَّنَّهُمْ عَنِ الْهُدَى ("I will surely lead them astray from guidance"). (وَلَأُمَنِّيَنَّهُمْ): [with] falsehood. (وَلَآمُرَنَّهُمْ): [to] misguidance.

ukberi-tibyan:120-120.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَعِدُهُمْ وَيُمَنِّيهِمْ وَمَا يَعِدُهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ إِلَّا غُرُورًا) (١٢٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَعِدُهُمْ): the second object is omitted, i.e. يَعِدُهُمُ النَّصْرَ وَالسَّلَامَةَ ("he promises them victory and safety"). Al-Aʿmash read it with the dāl quiescent; that is a lightening because of the multitude of vowels.

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ شِقَاقَ بَيْنِهِمَا فَابْعَثُوا حَكَمًا مِنْ أَهْلِهِ وَحَكَمًا مِنْ أَهْلِهَا إِنْ يُرِيدَا إِصْلَاحًا يُوَفِّقِ اللَّهُ بَيْنَهُمَا إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا خَبِيرًا) (٣٥).
His saying: (شِقَاقَ بَيْنِهِمَا): الشِّقَاق is discord; therefore its being put in a genitive construct with بَيْن is good, and بَيْن here is the bond existing between the two spouses. (حَكَمًا مِنْ أَهْلِهِ): مِنْ may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «ابْعَثُوا», so that the beginning [denoted by مِنْ] is the starting point of the sending. It may also be an adjective of the arbiter, and so be attached to something omitted. (إِنْ يُرِيدَا): the dual pronoun refers back to the two arbiters. It is also said: to the two spouses. So on the first, and the second, his saying يُوَفِّقِ اللَّهُ بَيْنَهُمَا refers to the two spouses. [Translator's note: the sentence is elliptical in the source; the sense appears to be that on either view the dual in يُوَفِّقِ اللَّهُ بَيْنَهُمَا refers to the spouses.]

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَلَا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئًا وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا وَبِذِي الْقُرْبَى وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَالْجَارِ ذِي الْقُرْبَى وَالْجَارِ الْجُنُبِ وَالصَّاحِبِ بِالْجَنْبِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ وَمَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ مَنْ كَانَ مُخْتَالًا فَخُورًا) (٣٦).
His saying: (وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا): on the accusative of «إِحْسَانًا» there are views which we mentioned in al-Baqara at His saying: (وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ).
(الْجُنُبِ): read with two ḍammas, and it is an adjective, like نَاقَةٌ أُجُدٌ ("a sturdy she-camel") and يَدٌ سُجُحٌ ("a gentle hand"). It is also read with fatḥa on the jīm and sukūn on the nūn [الْجَنْب], and that too is an adjective, meaning "the one who is at a distance", and it is like your saying رَجُلٌ عَدْلٌ ("a just man"). (وَالصَّاحِبِ بِالْجَنْبِ): the bāʾ may mean فِي ("in"), or it may have its usual meaning; on both views it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الصَّاحِب, and what governs it is the omitted element.

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
