Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ وَيَأْمُرُونَ النَّاسَ بِالْبُخْلِ وَيَكْتُمُونَ مَا آتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابًا مُهِينًا) (٣٧).
His saying: الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ: there are two views. First: it is accusative as a badal (substitute) from «مَنْ» in His saying (مَنْ كَانَ مُخْتَالًا فَخُورًا), and it is plural according to the meaning of مَنْ. It may also be taken with His saying مُخْتَالًا فَخُورًا, which is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and it is plural according to the meaning as well; or it is on the implication of "I censure" (أَذُمُّ). Second: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "are hated" (مُبْغَضُونَ), indicated by what preceded in His saying لَا يُحِبُّ. The khabar may also be "will be punished", because of His saying (وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابًا مُهِينًا). The implied form may also be "they are those who…". It may also be a mubtadaʾ, with وَالَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ conjoined to it, and the khabar «إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَظْلِمُ», i.e. "does not wrong them". البُخْل and البَخَل are two dialectal forms, and both have been read; and there are two further dialectal forms: البُخُل with ḍamma on the khāʾ and the bāʾ, and البَخْل with fatḥa on the bāʾ and sukūn on the khāʾ. (مِنْ فَضْلِهِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَا» or from the omitted pronoun referring back.

ukberi-tibyan:38-38.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ رِئَاءَ النَّاسِ وَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَلَا بِالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَمَنْ يَكُنِ الشَّيْطَانُ لَهُ قَرِينًا فَسَاءَ قَرِينًا) (٣٨).
His saying: (وَالَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ رِئَاءَ النَّاسِ): «رِئَاءَ» is a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose), and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is put in construct with its object. On this view His saying «وَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ» is conjoined to يُنْفِقُونَ and included in the ṣila (relative clause). It may also be a fresh (resumptive) clause. «رِئَاءَ النَّاسِ» may also be a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "they spend, showing off".
(فَسَاءَ قَرِينًا): i.e. "evil is he", and the pronoun refers back to مَنْ or to the devil; قَرِينًا is a tamyīz (specification). سَاءَ here is transferred to the category of نِعْمَ and بِئْسَ, so its agent and the noun specified for blame after it are like the agent of بِئْسَ and its specified noun; the implied form being "evil is the devil as a companion".
As for His saying (وَالَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ), there are three views on its position. First: it is genitive, conjoined to الْكَافِرِينَ in His saying (وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ). Second: accusative on the same basis as الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ is accusative. Third: nominative on the same basis as الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ is nominative; and both have been mentioned. As for «رِئَاءَ النَّاسِ», we have mentioned that it is a mafʿūl lahu or a ḥāl from the agent of يُنْفِقُونَ. It may also be a ḥāl from الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ, i.e. from the relative noun; on this view His saying «وَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ» is a fresh clause, so that one part of the ṣila is not separated from another by a ḥāl of the relative noun.

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted said: {وماذا عَلَيْهِم لَو آمنُوا بِاللَّه وَالْيَوْم الآخر وأنفقوا من مَا رزقهم الله وَكَانَ الله بهم عليما}
His saying: (وَمَاذَا عَلَيْهِمْ): there are two views. First: «مَا» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «ذَا» means الَّذِي ("which"), and عَلَيْهِمْ is its ṣila (relative clause); الَّذِي with its ṣila is the khabar (predicate) of مَا.
Some permitted الَّذِي with its ṣila to be the mubtadaʾ and مَا a fronted khabar, the khabar being fronted because it is interrogative.
Second: that مَا and ذَا are a single noun, a mubtadaʾ, and عَلَيْهِمْ is the khabar. We have mentioned this in al-Baqara more fully than here. (لَوْ): there are two views. First: it has its usual meaning, and the statement is construed according to the meaning, i.e. "if they had believed, it would not have harmed them". Second: that it means the أَنْ that puts the verb in the accusative, as we mentioned at His saying (لَوْ يُعَمَّرُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ) and elsewhere.
It may also mean the conditional إِنْ, as occurs in His saying (وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ), i.e. "and what would be against them if they believed?"; and its implied form on the other view is "what would be against them in believing?".

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَظْلِمُ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ وَإِنْ تَكُ حَسَنَةً يُضَاعِفْهَا وَيُؤْتِ مِنْ لَدُنْهُ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا) (٤٠).
His saying: (مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ): there are two views. First: it is an object of يَظْلِمُ, the implied form being "He does not wrong them" or "does not wrong anyone", with يَظْلِمُ meaning "diminishes", i.e. "reduces", and it is transitive to two objects. Second: it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "a wrong the size of an atom's weight"; the maṣdar and its adjective were omitted, and the muḍāf ilayhi was put in their place. [Translator's note: so in the source; it is the muḍāf (مِثْقَال) that stands in their place.] (وَإِنْ تَكُ حَسَنَةً): the nūn of تَكُنْ was dropped because of the frequency of use of this word, and because the nūn, with its nasality and sukūn, resembles the wāw; if it is vowelled it is not dropped, as in (وَمَنْ يَكُنِ الشَّيْطَانُ) and (لَمْ يَكُنِ الَّذِينَ). «حَسَنَةً» is in the nominative on the basis that kāna is complete (tāmma), and in the accusative on the basis that it is the incomplete (nāqiṣa) one. «مِنْ لَدُنْهُ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يُؤْتِ, or is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْأَجْر.

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جِئْنَا مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ بِشَهِيدٍ وَجِئْنَا بِكَ عَلَى هَؤُلَاءِ شَهِيدًا) (٤١).
His saying: (فَكَيْفَ إِذَا): what puts it [كَيْفَ] in the accusative is omitted, i.e. "how will you act" or "how will you be", and إِذَا is an adverb (ẓarf) for that omitted element. (مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to جِئْنَا, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from شَهِيد, according to those who permit the ḥāl of a genitive noun to precede it. (وَجِئْنَا بِكَ): conjoined to the first جِئْنَا. It may also be a ḥāl, with قَدْ intended; and it may be a fresh (resumptive) clause, with the past having the meaning of the future. (شَهِيدًا): a ḥāl, and «عَلَى» is attached to it; it [عَلَى هَؤُلَاءِ] may also be a ḥāl from it.

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَئِذٍ يَوَدُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَعَصَوُا الرَّسُولَ لَوْ تُسَوَّى بِهِمُ الْأَرْضُ وَلَا يَكْتُمُونَ اللَّهَ حَدِيثًا) (٤٢).
His saying: (يَوْمَئِذٍ): there are two views. First: it is an adverb (ẓarf) for «يَوَدُّ», which governs it. Second: it is governed by شَهِيدًا; on this view يَوَدُّ is an adjective of يَوْم, with the pronoun referring back omitted, i.e. "in it"; this was mentioned at His saying (وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمًا لَا تَجْزِي).
The origin of «إِذَا» [Translator's note: so in the source; the word discussed is إِذٍ in يَوْمَئِذٍ] is إِذْ, which is an adverb of past time; here it has been used for the future, and this is frequent in the Quran. They added the tanwīn to it as a compensation for the omitted clause, its implied form being "on the day when you bring the witnesses"; and the dhāl was given kasra because of its sukūn and the sukūn of the tanwīn after it. (وَعَصَوُا الرَّسُولَ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), with قَدْ intended, and it is parenthetical between يَوَدُّ and its object, which is «لَوْ تُسَوَّى». (لَوْ) has the meaning of maṣdariyya أَنْ, and تُسَوَّى is passive (lit. "that whose agent is not named"). It is also read تَسَّوَّى with fatḥa and doubling, i.e. تَتَسَوَّى, the second [tāʾ] being changed into sīn and assimilated; and it is read also without doubling [تَسَوَّى], with the second [tāʾ] dropped. (وَلَا يَكْتُمُونَ): there are two views. First: it is a ḥāl, and the implied form is "they wish that they had been punished in this world rather than the Hereafter, or that they were like the earth". (وَلَا يَكْتُمُونَ اللَّهَ): on that day «حَدِيثًا». [Translator's note: the second of the two views is not stated in the source as printed; the text appears to be defective here.]

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَأَنْتُمْ سُكَارَى حَتَّى تَعْلَمُوا مَا تَقُولُونَ وَلَا جُنُبًا إِلَّا عَابِرِي سَبِيلٍ حَتَّى تَغْتَسِلُوا وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ مَرْضَى أَوْ عَلَى سَفَرٍ أَوْ جَاءَ أَحَدٌ مِنْكُمْ مِنَ الْغَائِطِ أَوْ لَامَسْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا مَاءً فَتَيَمَّمُوا صَعِيدًا طَيِّبًا فَامْسَحُوا بِوُجُوهِكُمْ وَأَيْدِيكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَفُوًّا غَفُورًا) (٤٣).
His saying: (لَا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلَاةَ): it is said that what is meant is the places of prayer, and the muḍāf was omitted. It is also said: there is no ellipsis in it. (وَأَنْتُمْ سُكَارَى): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in تَقْرَبُوا. (سُكَارَى) is the plural of سَكْرَانُ ("drunk"); the sīn may take ḍamma or fatḥa, and both have been read. It was also read «سُكْرَى» with ḍamma on the sīn and without alif, and with fatḥa likewise [سَكْرَى]; this is a singular adjective standing in place of the plural: سُكْرَى is like حُبْلَى and سَكْرَى like عَطْشَى. (حَتَّى تَعْلَمُوا): i.e. "until (إِلَى أَنْ)", and it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to تَقْرَبُوا. (مَا): means الَّذِي ("that which") or is an indefinite qualified noun, with the pronoun referring back omitted; it may also be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), with no ellipsis. (وَلَا جُنُبًا): a ḥāl, the implied form being "do not pray in a state of major impurity", or "do not approach the places of prayer in a state of major impurity". In the most eloquent usage الْجُنُب is kept singular with the dual and the plural, being treated like description by maṣdars; and some of the Arabs make it dual and plural, saying جُنُبَانِ and أَجْنَابٌ. Its derivation is from al-mujānaba, which is keeping at a distance.
(إِلَّا عَابِرِي سَبِيلٍ): this too is a ḥāl, the implied form being "do not approach it in the state of major impurity except in the state of travel, or of passing through the mosque", according to the disagreement of people over what is meant by it. (حَتَّى تَغْتَسِلُوا): attached to what governs جُنُب. (مِنْكُمْ): an adjective of أَحَد. «مِنَ الْغَائِطِ» is the object of جَاءَ. The majority read الْغَائِط on the pattern fāʿil; the verb from it is غَاطَ الْمَكَانُ يَغُوطُ, said when a place is low-lying. Ibn Masʿūd read it with a vowelless yāʾ and without alif [الْغَيْط], and there are two views on it. First: it is the maṣdar of يَغُوطُ; the regular form would have been غَوْطًا, but the wāw was changed into yāʾ, made vowelless, and the letter before it given fatḥa, for lightness. Second: that he meant الْغَيِّط, which was lightened, like سَيِّد and مَيِّت. (أَوْ لَمَسْتُمْ): read without alif and with alif [لَامَسْتُمْ], and the two have the same meaning. It is also said: لَامَسْتُمْ is for what falls short of intercourse, and لَمَسْتُمُ for intercourse. (فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا): the fāʾ conjoined what follows it to جَاءَ, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is «فَتَيَمَّمُوا»; «جَاءَ» is conjoined to كُنْتُمْ, i.e. "and if anyone comes". (صَعِيدًا): the object of تَيَمَّمُوا, i.e. "aim for clean earth". It is also said: it is on the implied omission of the bāʾ, i.e. "with (بِ) clean earth". (بِوُجُوهِكُمْ): the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "wipe your faces", and there is an ellipsis in the phrase, i.e. "then wipe your faces with it" or "from it"; this appears overtly in the verse of al-Māʾida.

ukberi-tibyan:121-121.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُولَئِكَ مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَلَا يَجِدُونَ عَنْهَا مَحِيصًا) (١٢١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ): [Translator's note: so in the text; the discussion that follows concerns عَنْهَا in this verse.] It is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَحِيصًا», the implied wording being مَحِيصًا عَنْهَا ("an escape from it"); المَحِيص is a maṣdar (verbal noun), so it cannot validly govern what precedes it. عَنْهَا may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, and that is what is called tabyīn ("clarification"), i.e. "[I mean] from it". [Translator's note: the text glosses this as غِنًى عَنْهَا, literally "independence from it".] It is not permissible for it to be attached to يَجِدُونَ, because that verb is not made transitive with عَنْ. The mīm in المَحِيص is augmentative, and it is from حَاصَ يَحِيصُ, "he escaped".

ukberi-tibyan:122-122.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ سَنُدْخِلُهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقًّا وَمَنْ أَصْدَقُ مِنَ اللَّهِ قِيلًا) (١٢٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is (سَنُدْخِلُهُمْ). It may also be in the position of the accusative by an omitted verb explained by what follows it, i.e. وَنُدْخِلُ الَّذِينَ ("and We shall admit those who…").
And (وَعْدَ اللَّهِ): accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because His saying سَنُدْخِلُهُمْ is equivalent to وَعَدَهُمْ ("He promised them"). And (حَقًّا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the maṣdar; it may also be the maṣdar of an omitted verb, i.e. حَقَّ ذَلِكَ حَقًّا ("that is truly true").

ukberi-tibyan:123-123.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَيْسَ بِأَمَانِيِّكُمْ وَلَا أَمَانِيِّ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ مَنْ يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا يُجْزَ بِهِ وَلَا يَجِدْ لَهُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَلِيًّا وَلَا نَصِيرًا) (١٢٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَيْسَ بِأَمَانِيِّكُمْ): the noun (ism) of لَيْسَ is implied within it; it has not been mentioned beforehand, but the occasion of the verse indicates it. That is, the Jews said, "We are the people of Paradise", the Christians said the same, and the idolaters said, "We will not be resurrected". So He said لَيْسَ بِأَمَانِيِّكُمْ, i.e. "what you have claimed is not [according to your wishes]".

ukberi-tibyan:124-124.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصَّالِحَاتِ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَى وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَأُولَئِكَ يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ وَلَا يُظْلَمُونَ نَقِيرًا) (١٢٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَى): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); concerning the one to whom it refers there are two views. First: the agent pronoun in يَعْمَلُ. Second: مِنَ الصَّالِحَاتِ, i.e. "being from a male or a female", or "occurring [from them]". The first مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida) according to al-Akhfash, and an adjective according to Sībawayh, i.e. "something of the righteous deeds". وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ is also a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:125-125.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ دِينًا مِمَّنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ لِلَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ وَاتَّبَعَ مِلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفًا وَاتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ خَلِيلًا) (١٢٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِمَّنْ أَسْلَمَ): أَحْسَنُ governs it; it is like your saying زَيْدٌ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ عَمْرٍو ("Zayd is more excellent than ʿAmr"), i.e. "he surpasses ʿAmr". And (لِلَّهِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَسْلَمَ; it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «وَجْهِهِ». (وَاتَّبَعَ): conjoined to أَسْلَمَ.
And (حَنِيفًا): a ḥāl; it has been discussed in al-Baqara. Here it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in اتَّبَعَ. (وَاتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ): resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:127-127.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَسْتَفْتُونَكَ فِي النِّسَاءِ قُلِ اللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ وَمَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ فِي يَتَامَى النِّسَاءِ اللَّاتِي لَا تُؤْتُونَهُنَّ مَا كُتِبَ لَهُنَّ وَتَرْغَبُونَ أَنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ وَالْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الْوِلْدَانِ وَأَنْ تَقُومُوا لِلْيَتَامَى بِالْقِسْطِ وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِهِ عَلِيمًا) (١٢٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا يُتْلَى): concerning «مَا» there are several views. First: its position is genitive, conjoined to the pronoun made genitive by فِي; this is according to the view of the Kufans, because they permit conjoining to a genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition. Second: that it is in the position of the accusative according to the sense "and We make clear to you what is recited", because the meaning of يُفْتِيكُمْ is "He makes clear to you". Third: it is in the position of the nominative, and this is the preferred view. In this there are three views. First: it is conjoined to the agent pronoun in يُفْتِيكُمْ, the preposition and its genitive noun functioning like a tawkīd (emphasis). Second: it is conjoined to the name of Allah, namely قُلِ اللَّهُ. Third: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar (predicate) omitted, its implied form being "and what is recited to you in the Book makes clear to you". «فِي» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يُتْلَى, and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يُتْلَى. And (فِي يَتَامَى): its implied form is "[concerning] the ruling on the orphans". So the second فِي is attached to what the first is attached to, because its meaning is different: the first is adverbial, and the second has the meaning of the bāʾ, i.e. "because of the orphans", just as you say جِئْتُكَ فِي يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ فِي أَمْرِ زَيْدٍ ("I came to you on Friday about Zayd's affair"). It is also said: the second is a badal (substitute) from the first. The second may also be attached to الْكِتَاب, i.e. "what was written concerning the ruling on the orphans". And the first may be adverbial and the second a ḥāl, in which case it is attached to something omitted. And (يَتَامَى النِّسَاءِ): i.e. "concerning the orphans among them". The Kufans said: the implied wording is فِي النِّسَاءِ الْيَتَامَى ("concerning the orphan women"), so the adjective was put in construct with the qualified noun. It is also read فِي يَيَامَى, with two yāʾs; the original is أَيَامَى, and the hamza was changed into yāʾ, just as they said "So-and-so ibn Aʿṣur" and "Yaʿṣur". Concerning الْأَيَامَى there is discussion which we will mention in its place, if Allah wills.
(وَتَرْغَبُونَ): there are two views about it. First: it is conjoined to تُؤْتُونَ, the implied wording being وَلَا تَرْغَبُونَ ("and you do not desire"). Second: it is a ḥāl, i.e. "while you desire to marry them". (وَالْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ): in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the genitive pronoun in «يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ», and likewise «وَأَنْ تَقُومُوا»; this too is conjoining to a genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition, and the Kufans have mentioned it. It may also be in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the position of فِيهِنَّ, the implied wording being "and He makes clear to you the situation of the oppressed"; with this implied wording it fits the school of the Basrans without strain. The good view is that it is conjoined to يَتَامَى النِّسَاءِ, and أَنْ تَقُومُوا is also conjoined to it, i.e. "and concerning your standing [for the orphans in justice]".

ukberi-tibyan:128-128.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ مِنْ بَعْلِهَا نُشُوزًا أَوْ إِعْرَاضًا فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا أَنْ يُصْلِحَا بَيْنَهُمَا صُلْحًا وَالصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ وَأُحْضِرَتِ الْأَنْفُسُ الشُّحَّ وَإِنْ تُحْسِنُوا وَتَتَّقُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا) (١٢٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِنِ امْرَأَةٌ): امْرَأَةٌ is nominative by an omitted verb, i.e. وَإِنْ خَافَتِ امْرَأَةٌ ("and if a woman fears"); the mentioned «خَافَتْ» makes it unnecessary.
The Kufans said: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows it is the khabar (predicate). In our view this is a mistake, because the conditional particle has no meaning with respect to a noun, so it [i.e. making the noun a mubtadaʾ after it] contradicts [its requirement of] the verb; that is why the verb comes in the jussive after the noun in the saying of ʿAdī:
وَمَتَى وَاغِلٌ يَنُبْهُمْ يُحَيُّو هُ وَتُعْطَفْ عَلَيْهِ كَأْسُ السَّاقِي
("Whenever an uninvited drinker comes upon them, they greet him, and the cupbearer's cup is turned towards him")
[Translator's note: the bracketed words above are added for clarity; the Arabic reads literally "so it is contradictory to the verb".]
(مِنْ بَعْلِهَا): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to خَافَتْ, and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «نُشُوزًا».
And (صُلْحًا): on this [reading] it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) occupying the place of تُصَالِحُ ("reconciling with one another"). The implied wording may also be أَنْ يَصَّالَحَا فَيُصْلِحَا صُلْحًا ("that they reconcile with one another and so make a reconciliation").
It is also read with doubling of the ṣād and without alif (يَصَّلِحَا); its original form is يَصْطَلِحَا, and the tāʾ was changed into ṣād and the first [ṣād] was assimilated into it.
(يَصْطَلِحَا) has also been read, with the tāʾ changed into ṭāʾ; and (صُلْحًا) on both of these is in the place of اصْطِلَاحٍ ("mutual reconciliation"). It has also been read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and the ṣād quiescent (يُصْلِحَا), its past being أَصْلَحَ.
On this reading there are two views concerning (صُلْحًا).
First: it is a maṣdar in the place of إِصْلَاحٍ ("setting right"), and the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is بَيْنَهُمَا; or [بَيْنَهُمَا] may be an adverbial, with the object omitted.
Second: that صُلْحًا is a mafʿūl bihi, and بَيْنَهُمَا is an adverbial or a ḥāl from صَلُحَ. [Translator's note: so in the text; presumably "from صُلْحًا" is intended.] (وَأُحْضِرَتِ الْأَنْفُسُ الشُّحَّ): أُحْضِرَتْ is transitive to two objects; you say أَحْضَرْتُ زَيْدًا الطَّعَامَ ("I brought Zayd to the food"). The first object is الْأَنْفُسُ, and it is what stands in place of the fāʿil (agent). This verb is transferred by the hamza from حَضَرَ, and حَضَرَ is transitive to one object, as in their saying حَضَرَ الْقَاضِي الْيَوْمَ امْرَأَةٌ ("a woman came before the judge today").

ukberi-tibyan:129-129.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعُوا أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا بَيْنَ النِّسَاءِ وَلَوْ حَرَصْتُمْ فَلَا تَمِيلُوا كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ فَتَذَرُوهَا كَالْمُعَلَّقَةِ وَإِنْ تُصْلِحُوا وَتَتَّقُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا) (١٢٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ): «كُلَّ» is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because it takes the status of what it is annexed to: if it is annexed to a maṣdar it is a maṣdar, and if it is annexed to an adverbial it is an adverbial. (فَتَذَرُوهَا): the answer to the prohibition, so it is accusative; it may also be conjoined to تَمِيلُوا, in which case it is jussive (majzūm). (كَالْمُعَلَّقَةِ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:131-131.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَقَدْ وَصَّيْنَا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ أَنِ اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَإِنْ تَكْفُرُوا فَإِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَنِيًّا حَمِيدًا) (١٣١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِيَّاكُمْ): conjoined to الَّذِينَ; the rule for a conjoined pronoun is that it be detached. And (أَنِ اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ): in the position of the accusative according to Sībawayh, and of the genitive according to al-Khalīl; the implied wording is بِأَنِ اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ("that you fear Allah"), and on this view أَنْ is maṣdarī. It may also have the meaning of أَيْ ("namely"), because وَصَّيْنَا carries the meaning of saying, so it can validly be explained by the explicative أَيْ.

ukberi-tibyan:44-45.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا نَصِيبًا مِنَ الْكِتَابِ يَشْتَرُونَ الضَّلَالَةَ وَيُرِيدُونَ أَنْ تَضِلُّوا السَّبِيلَ (٤٤) وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِأَعْدَائِكُمْ وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ وَلِيًّا وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ نَصِيرًا (٤٥)).
His saying: (مِنَ الْكِتَابِ): an adjective of نَصِيب. (يَشْتَرُونَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent in أُوتُوا. «وَيُرِيدُونَ» is like it; and if you wish you may make them two ḥāls from the relative noun, namely His saying «مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has إِلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا], and it is an anticipated (muqaddara) ḥāl. One says ضَلَلْتُ «السَّبِيلَ» and ضَلَلْتُ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ ("I strayed from the way"), and it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), not an adverb (ẓarf); it is like your saying أَخْطَأَ الطَّرِيقَ ("he missed the road"). (وَلِيًّا) and (نَصِيرًا): both accusative as tamyīz (specification). It is also said: as ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مِنَ الَّذِينَ هَادُوا يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ عَنْ مَوَاضِعِهِ وَيَقُولُونَ سَمِعْنَا وَعَصَيْنَا وَاسْمَعْ غَيْرَ مُسْمَعٍ وَرَاعِنَا لَيًّا بِأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ وَطَعْنًا فِي الدِّينِ وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا وَاسْمَعْ وَانْظُرْنَا لَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَهُمْ وَأَقْوَمَ وَلَكِنْ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِكُفْرِهِمْ فَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا) (٤٦).
His saying: (مِنَ الَّذِينَ هَادُوا): there are three views. First: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), and on this there are two interpretations. One: its implied form is "they are of those who…", so «يُحَرِّفُونَ» on this view is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent in هَادُوا. The other: its implied form is "among those who are Jews are a people (قَوْمٌ)", so قَوْمٌ is the mubtadaʾ and what precedes it is the khabar, and يُحَرِّفُونَ is a naʿt (adjective) of قَوْمٌ. It is also said: the implied form is "among those who are Jews are some who (مَنْ) distort", as He said: (وَمَا مِنَّا إِلَّا لَهُ), i.e. "except one who (مَنْ) has…". In our view this مَنْ is an indefinite qualified noun like قَوْمٌ, not meaning الَّذِي, because a relative noun is not omitted while its ṣila (relative clause) is kept. The second view: that مِنَ الَّذِينَ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to نَصِير, so it is in the accusative position by it, as He said: (فَمَنْ يَنْصُرُنَا مِنْ بَأْسِ اللَّهِ), i.e. "protects us". The third: that it is a ḥāl from the agent in يُرِيدُونَ. It may not be a ḥāl from the pronoun in أُوتُوا, because one thing does not have more than one ḥāl unless some of the ḥāls are conjoined to others; nor is it a ḥāl from الَّذِينَ, for this same reason. It is also said: it is a ḥāl from أَعْدَائِكُمْ, i.e. "and Allah knows best your enemies, being from among those who…", and the parenthetical separation between them is reinforcing, so it does not prevent the ḥāl. In every place where مِنَ الَّذِينَ هَادُوا is made a ḥāl, يُحَرِّفُونَ in it is a ḥāl from the agent in هَادُوا. (الْكَلِمَ): the plural of كَلِمَة. It is also read «الْكَلَامَ», and the meaning is close. (عَنْ مَوَاضِعِهِ): attached to يُحَرِّفُونَ; the pronoun in the genitive construct is masculine, being construed according to the meaning of الْكَلِم, because it is a collective (jins). (وَيَقُولُونَ): conjoined to يُحَرِّفُونَ. (غَيْرَ مُسْمَعٍ): a ḥāl, and the second object is omitted, i.e. "may you not be made to hear anything disliked"; this is the outward sense of their saying, but what they intended is "may you not be made to hear any good". It is also said: they meant "not listened to (by us) from you". (وَرَاعِنَا): this was mentioned in al-Baqara. (لَيًّا) and (وَطَعْنًا): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). It is also said: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl. The original of لَيّ is لَوْي; the wāw was changed into yāʾ and assimilated. (فِي الدِّينِ): attached to «طَعْن». (خَيْرًا لَهُمْ): it may have the meaning of afʿal (the elative), as He said «وَأَقْوَمَ», with مِنْ omitted, i.e. "than something else"; and it may mean "excellent, good", so it does not need «مِنْ». (إِلَّا قَلِيلًا): an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a little belief".

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ آمِنُوا بِمَا نَزَّلْنَا مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا مَعَكُمْ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَطْمِسَ وُجُوهًا فَنَرُدَّهَا عَلَى أَدْبَارِهَا أَوْ نَلْعَنَهُمْ كَمَا لَعَنَّا أَصْحَابَ السَّبْتِ وَكَانَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ مَفْعُولًا) (٤٧).
His saying: (مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَطْمِسَ]: attached (mutaʿalliq) to آمِنُوا. (عَلَى أَدْبَارِهَا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of الْوُجُوه, and it is an anticipated (muqaddara) ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُوِّنَ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَمَنْ يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدِ افْتَرَى إِثْمًا عَظِيمًا) (٤٨).
His saying: (وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ): it is a fresh (resumptive) clause, not conjoined to the first يَغْفِرُ, because if it were conjoined to it, it would become negated.

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ بَلِ اللَّهُ يُزَكِّي مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَلَا يُظْلَمُونَ فَتِيلًا) (٤٩).
His saying: (بَلِ اللَّهُ يُزَكِّي مَنْ يَشَاءُ): its implied form is "they erred; rather, Allah purifies…". (وَلَا يُظْلَمُونَ): the plural pronoun refers back to the meaning of مَنْ; and it may be a fresh (resumptive) clause, i.e. [referring to both] whoever purified himself and whomever Allah purified. (فَتِيلًا): like «مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ» in its i'rab, and that has been mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:50-50.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (انْظُرْ كَيْفَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ وَكَفَى بِهِ إِثْمًا مُبِينًا) (٥٠).
His saying: (كَيْفَ يَفْتَرُونَ): كَيْفَ is accusative by يَفْتَرُونَ, and the position of the whole statement is accusative by انْظُرُوا [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has انْظُرْ].
(عَلَى اللَّهِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to يَفْتَرُونَ. It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الْكَذِبَ». It may not be attached to الْكَذِب, because what a maṣdar governs does not precede it; but if it is taken as clarification (tabyīn), it is permissible.

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا نَصِيبًا مِنَ الْكِتَابِ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْجِبْتِ وَالطَّاغُوتِ وَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هَؤُلَاءِ أَهْدَى مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا سَبِيلًا) (٥١).
His saying: (هَؤُلَاءِ أَهْدَى): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the accusative position by يَقُولُونَ. (لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): specification and clarification, also attached (mutaʿalliq) to يَقُولُونَ. (يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْجِبْتِ) and (وَيَقُولُونَ) are like يَشْتَرُونَ الضَّلَالَةَ and وَيُرِيدُونَ, and that has been mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَمْ لَهُمْ نَصِيبٌ مِنَ الْمُلْكِ فَإِذًا لَا يُؤْتُونَ النَّاسَ نَقِيرًا) (٥٣).
His saying: (أَمْ لَهُمْ نَصِيبٌ): أَمْ is the disjoined (munqaṭiʿa) one, i.e. "nay, do they have…?"; and likewise «أَمْ يَحْسُدُونَ».
(فَإِذَنْ): a particle that puts the verb in the accusative when the verb depends on it; it has places in which it is cancelled (made inoperative), and among the governors of verbs it resembles ظَنَنْتُ among the governors of nouns. The nūn in it is radical, not tanwīn; for this reason it is written with nūn, though al-Farrāʾ permitted it to be written with alif. It did not govern here because of the conjunction, namely the fāʾ; outside the Quran it may govern together with the fāʾ. What cancels its governing is not لَا, because a governor reaches past لَا.

ukberi-tibyan:55-56.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ آمَنَ بِهِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ صَدَّ عَنْهُ وَكَفَى بِجَهَنَّمَ سَعِيرًا (٥٥) إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِنَا سَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِمْ نَارًا كُلَّمَا نَضِجَتْ جُلُودُهُمْ بَدَّلْنَاهُمْ جُلُودًا غَيْرَهَا لِيَذُوقُوا الْعَذَابَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا) (٥٦).
His saying: (مَنْ آمَنَ بِهِ): the hāʾ refers back to the Book. It is also said: to Ibrāhīm. It is also said: to Muḥammad. (سَعِيرًا) means "blazing" (مُسْتَعِرًا). (نَضِجَتْ جُلُودُهُمْ): read with assimilation [of the tāʾ into the jīm], because both are letters of the middle of the mouth; and pronouncing them distinctly is the basic form. (بَدَّلْنَاهُمْ جُلُودًا): i.e. "with (بِ) skins". It is also said: it is transitive to the second object by itself.

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ سَنُدْخِلُهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا لَهُمْ فِيهَا أَزْوَاجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ وَنُدْخِلُهُمْ ظِلًّا ظَلِيلًا) (٥٧).
His saying: (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): it may be in the accusative position, conjoined to الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا, or nominative according to the position [of the noun of إِنَّ], or as a fresh (resumptive) clause, with the khabar (predicate) «سَنُدْخِلُهُمْ». (خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object in نُدْخِلُهُمْ, or from جَنَّات, because in both there is a pronoun of each of the two. It may also be an adjective of جَنَّات according to the view of the Kufans. (لَهُمْ فِيهَا أَزْوَاجٌ): a ḥāl, or an adjective.

ukberi-tibyan:58-58.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَنْ تُؤَدُّوا الْأَمَانَاتِ إِلَى أَهْلِهَا وَإِذَا حَكَمْتُمْ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ أَنْ تَحْكُمُوا بِالْعَدْلِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ نِعِمَّا يَعِظُكُمْ بِهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا) (٥٨).
His saying: (وَإِذَا حَكَمْتُمْ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ أَنْ تَحْكُمُوا بِالْعَدْلِ): there are two views on what governs إِذَا. First: an omitted verb, its implied form being "He commands you to judge when you judge", with the mentioned أَنْ تَحْكُمُوا made an explanation of the omitted element; so أَنْ تَحْكُمُوا has no grammatical position, because it explains the omitted element, and the omitted element is the object of يَأْمُرُكُمْ. أَنْ تَحْكُمُوا may not govern إِذَا, because what a maṣdar governs does not precede it.
The second view: that you put «إِذَا» in the accusative by يَأْمُرُكُمْ, and أَنْ تَحْكُمُوا likewise by it; the implied form being that the conjunction belongs with أَنْ تَحْكُمُوا, but the two are separated by the adverb, as in the saying of al-Aʿshā:
يَوْمَ يَرَاهَا كَشِبْهِ أَرْدِيَةِ الْـ ... عَصْبِ وَيَوْمًا أَدِيمُهَا نَغِلَا
("One day he sees it like the likeness of striped Yemeni cloaks, and one day its hide spoiled.")
(بِالْعَدْلِ): it may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial). (نِعِمَّا يَعِظُكُمْ بِهِ): the clause is the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ. In «مَا» there are three views. First: that it means "the thing", a complete definite noun, and يَعِظُكُمْ is an adjective of an omitted qualified noun, which is the one specified for praise; its implied form being "excellent is the thing: a thing with which He admonishes you". يَعِظُكُمْ may also be an adjective of an omitted accusative noun, i.e. "excellent is the thing as a thing with which He admonishes you", like your saying نِعْمَ الرَّجُلُ رَجُلًا صَالِحًا زَيْدٌ ("excellent is the man, as a righteous man, Zayd"); this is permitted by some grammarians, and the one specified for praise is omitted here. Second: that «مَا» means الَّذِي, what follows it is its ṣila (relative clause), and its position is nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of نِعْمَ, with the specified noun omitted, i.e. "excellent is that with which He admonishes you: the rendering of trusts and judging with justice". Third: that «مَا» is an indefinite qualified noun, the agent is latent, and the specified noun is omitted, as in His saying: (بِئْسَ لِلظَّالِمِينَ بَدَلًا).

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا وَنِسَاءً وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي تَسَاءَلُونَ بِهِ وَالْأَرْحَامَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا) (١).
The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He: (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ) has already passed at the beginning of al-Baqara. (مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ): in the position of the accusative by خَلَقَكُمْ, and مِنْ is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya); likewise «مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا».
(مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًا كَثِيرًا): [كَثِيرًا is] a naʿt (adjective) of رِجَالًا. It was not made feminine because it was construed according to the meaning, since رِجَالًا has the sense of "a number", "a kind" or "a group", just as the verb attributed to a group of females is made masculine, as in His saying: «وَقَالَ نِسْوَةٌ». It is also said: (كَثِيرًا) is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a great spreading" (بَثًّا كَثِيرًا).
(تَسَاءَلُونَ): it is read with doubling of the sīn (تَسَّاءَلُونَ); the origin is تَتَسَاءَلُونَ, and the second tāʾ was changed into sīn to avoid repeating the same letter, the tāʾ resembling the sīn in being voiceless (hams). It is read without doubling, with the second tāʾ dropped, because the remaining one indicates it. The preposition entered upon the object because the meaning is "you swear oaths to one another by Him".
(وَالْأَرْحَامَ): it is read in the accusative, and there are two views on it:
The first: it is conjoined to the name of Allah, i.e. "and fear [to sever] the wombs [i.e. ties of kinship], lest you cut them". The second: it is construed on the position of the preposition and its genitive noun, as you say مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ وَعَمْرًا ("I passed by Zayd, and ʿAmr"); the implied form is: "the One whom you hold in reverence, and the wombs", because swearing by Him is reverence for Him. It is also read in the genitive (وَالْأَرْحَامِ). It is said that it is conjoined to the genitive [pronoun]; this is not permissible according to the Basrans, and it has come only in poetry, despite its ugliness; the Kufans permitted it, though as weak.
It is also said that the genitive is by way of oath; this too is weak, because reports have come forbidding swearing by one's forefathers, and because the implied form in the oath would be "and by the Lord of the wombs", and this has been made unnecessary by what precedes it.
It has also been read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, in the nominative (وَالْأَرْحَامُ); it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar (predicate) omitted, its implied form being: "and the wombs are inviolable", or "their sanctity is obligatory".

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَآتُوا الْيَتَامَى أَمْوَالَهُمْ وَلَا تَتَبَدَّلُوا الْخَبِيثَ بِالطَّيِّبِ وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَهُمْ إِلَى أَمْوَالِكُمْ إِنَّهُ كَانَ حُوبًا كَبِيرًا) (٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِالطَّيِّبِ): it is the second object of تَتَبَدَّلُوا. (إِلَى أَمْوَالِكُمْ): إِلَى is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, and it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "added to your wealth". It is also said that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) according to the meaning, because the meaning of "do not consume their wealth" is "do not add it". (إِنَّهُ): the hāʾ is the pronoun of the maṣdar (verbal noun) indicated by تَأْكُلُوا, i.e. "the consuming and taking is…". The majority read «حُوبًا» with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, and it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar); it is also said to be a maṣdar. It is read with fatḥa on it (حَوْبًا), and that is the maṣdar of حَابَ يَحُوبُ, when one sins.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا تُقْسِطُوا فِي الْيَتَامَى فَانْكِحُوا مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ مَثْنَى وَثُلَاثَ وَرُبَاعَ فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا فَوَاحِدَةً أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ ذَلِكَ أَدْنَى أَلَّا تَعُولُوا) (٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ): on the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of this condition there are two views:
The first: it is His saying «فَانْكِحُوا مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ…». It was made the apodosis only because they used to feel scruples about guardianship over the wealth of orphans, while not feeling scruples about taking many wives, even though injustice occurs among them when they are many; so it is as though He said: "if you feel scruples about this, then feel scruples about that".
The second view: that the apodosis is His saying فَوَاحِدَةً, because the meaning is: "if you fear that you will not act justly in marrying the orphan girls, then marry one of them"; then He repeated this meaning in His saying «فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَنْ لَا تَعْدِلُوا» because the separation between the first [condition] and its apodosis had become long. Abū ʿAlī mentioned this view.
(أَلَّا تُقْسِطُوا): the majority read it with ḍamma on the tāʾ, and it is from أَقْسَطَ, "to act justly". It was read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, with fatḥa on it (تَقْسِطُوا), which is from قَسَطَ, "to act unjustly", and لَا would then be redundant (zāʾida).
(مَا طَابَ): «مَا» here has the sense of مَنْ ("whoever"), and it has parallels in the Qurʾān which will come before you, if Allah the Exalted wills.
It is also said: مَا is used for the attributes of rational beings, and it is so here, because مَا طَابَ indicates the good ones among them.
It is also said: it is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, its implied form being: "marry a good kind that is pleasing to you", or "a number that is pleasing to you". It is also said: it is maṣdariyya, and the maṣdar (verbal noun) implied by it together with the verb is to be understood as an active participle, i.e. "marry the good [ones]".
(مِنَ النِّسَاءِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in طَابَ.
(مَثْنَى وَثُلَاثَ وَرُبَاعَ): indefinite nouns that are diptotes because of deflection (ʿadl) and descriptive quality; they are a badal (substitute) from مَا. It is also said that they are a ḥāl from النِّسَاء. It is read irregularly
«وَرُبَعَ» without alif; the reasoning for it is that the alif was dropped, as it was dropped in خِيَمٌ, the original being خِيَامٌ, and as it was dropped in their saying أَمْ وَاللَّهِ [for أَمَا وَاللَّهِ].
The wāw in «وَثُلَاثَ وَرُبَاعَ» is not the conjunction that requires combining [them] at one time, because if it were so it would be a faltering of speech, since it is among the feeblest of expressions to break down the number nine in this way; and also because the meaning would not be correct, since مَثْنَى does not express two only, but "two by two", and ثُلَاثَ "three by three"; and this meaning shows that what is intended is choice, not combination.
(فَوَاحِدَةً): i.e. "then marry one". It is read in the nominative (فَوَاحِدَةٌ), as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then the one married is one". The implied form may also be: "then one suffices" [Translator's note: the text writes تُكْفِي]. (أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ): أَوْ is for choice, in its usual sense; it may also be for permission (ibāḥa). «مَا» here is like مَا in His saying «مَا طَابَ». (أَلَّا تَعُولُوا): i.e. "nearer to your not inclining [to injustice]" (إِلَى أَنْ لَا تَعُولُوا); we have mentioned the like of it in the verse of debt.

ukberi-tibyan:135-135.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوِ الْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًا فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِهِمَا فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا الْهَوَى أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا) (١٣٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (شُهَدَاءَ): a second khabar (predicate). It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «قَوَّامِينَ». (عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to a verb indicated by «شُهَدَاءَ», i.e. وَلَوْ شَهِدْتُمْ ("even if you bear witness"); it may also be attached to قَوَّامِينَ. (إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا): the noun (ism) of كَانَ is implied within it, indicated by the previous mention of testimony, i.e. "if the opposing party is…", or "if each one of the person testified against and the person testified for is…".
Concerning (أَوِ) there are two views. First: it has the meaning of the wāw ("and"); this is reported from al-Akhfash. On this view the pronoun in بِهِمَا refers back to the words غَنِيٍّ and فَقِيرٍ. The second view: that «أَوْ» keeps its proper meaning, and here it is for detailing what was left vague in the speech. That is, each of the person testified against and the person testified for may be rich and may be poor: they may both be rich, they may both be poor, or one of them may be rich and the other poor. Since the divisions, when detailed, are thus, and they were not mentioned, He brought أَوْ to indicate this detailing. On this view the pronoun in بِهِمَا refers back to the person testified for and the person testified against, in whatever state they are, not to the description. It is also said: the pronoun refers back to what the speech indicates, the implied wording being "Allah is more entitled to the rich and the poor". It is also said: it refers back to the rich and the poor because the two nouns indicate it. (أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا): there are three views about it. First: its implied form is فِي أَنْ لَا تَعْدِلُوا, and لَا was omitted, i.e. "do not follow desire in abandoning justice". Second: its implied form is "seeking to deviate (تَعْدِلُوا) from the truth". Third: its implied form is "for fear of deviating from the truth". On the [last] two views it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا is read with two wāws, the first of them with ḍamma, from لَوَى يَلْوِي ("to twist"). It is also read with a single quiescent wāw (تَلُوا), and there are two views about it. First: its original is تَلْوُوا, as in the first reading, except that the wāw with ḍamma was changed into hamza and then its vowel was cast onto the lām; the like of this was mentioned in Āl ʿImrān. Second: that it is from وَلِيَ الشَّيْءَ ("he took charge of the thing"), i.e. "if you take charge of the judgement or turn away from it", or "if you take charge of the right in the judgement".

ukberi-tibyan:137-137.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا) (١٣٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ): this has been discussed at His saying (مَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيَذَرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ).

ukberi-tibyan:139-139.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا) (١٣٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَمِيعًا): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the preposition phrase, namely His saying لِلَّهِ.

ukberi-tibyan:140-140.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَدْ نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ أَنْ إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ يُكْفَرُ بِهَا وَيُسْتَهْزَأُ بِهَا فَلَا تَقْعُدُوا مَعَهُمْ حَتَّى يَخُوضُوا فِي حَدِيثٍ غَيْرِهِ إِنَّكُمْ إِذًا مِثْلُهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ جَامِعُ الْمُنَافِقِينَ وَالْكَافِرِينَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ جَمِيعًا) (١٤٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَقَدْ نَزَّلَ): it is read in the passive (with the agent unnamed); what stands in place of the fāʿil (agent) is «أَنْ» together with what completes it. أَنْ is the one lightened from the heavy form (أَنَّ), i.e. أَنَّهُ إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ ("that, when you hear the verses of Allah…").
«نَزَّلَ» is also read with the agent named, in which case أَنْ is in the position of the accusative. The gist of the meaning is: "He has sent down to you the prohibition against sitting with them when hearing disbelief from them". And (يُكْفَرُ بِهَا): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْآيَات. There is an omission in the phrase, its implied form being "someone disbelieves in them"; the agent was omitted and the preposition phrase was put in its place, and the pronoun in «مَعَهُمْ» refers back to the omitted [agent]. «فَلَا تَقْعُدُوا» is also construed according to the meaning, because the meaning of وَقَدْ نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ is "it has been said [to you]"; and the fāʾ is the response of إِذَا. (إِنَّكُمْ إِذًا مِثْلُهُمْ): إِذًا here is inoperative (mulghāh) because it occurs between the noun and the predicate; that is why no verb is mentioned after it. «مِثْلًا» is singular because it has the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun); like it is (أَنُؤْمِنُ لِبَشَرَيْنِ مِثْلِنَا), while it was made plural in His saying (ثُمَّ لَا يَكُونُوا أَمْثَالَكُمْ). It has been read, as an anomalous reading (shādhdh), «مِثْلَهُمْ» with fatḥa; it is indeclinable (mabnī) because it is annexed to an indeterminate word (mubham), just as it is indeclinable in His saying (مِثْلَ مَا أَنَّكُمْ تَنْطِقُونَ); this will be mentioned in its place, if Allah the Exalted wills.
It is also said: it is accusative as an adverbial, as was said concerning the verse of al-Farazdaq: وَإِذْ مَا مِثْلَهُمْ بَشَرُ ("since no human being is like them"), i.e. "you are in a state like theirs".

ukberi-tibyan:141-141.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ يَتَرَبَّصُونَ بِكُمْ فَإِنْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فَتْحٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ قَالُوا أَلَمْ نَكُنْ مَعَكُمْ وَإِنْ كَانَ لِلْكَافِرِينَ نَصِيبٌ قَالُوا أَلَمْ نَسْتَحْوِذْ عَلَيْكُمْ وَنَمْنَعْكُمْ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فَاللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَلَنْ يَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ سَبِيلًا) (١٤١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يَتَرَبَّصُونَ): in the position of the genitive as an adjective of الْمُنَافِقِينَ and الْكَافِرِينَ. It may be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. هُمْ ("they are"). It may be a mubtadaʾ, the khabar being «فَإِنْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فَتْحٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ» and what is connected to it. And it may be in the position of the accusative by an implied أَعْنِي ("I mean"). (نَسْتَحْوِذْ): it is anomalous with respect to analogy (qiyās); the analogical form is نَسْتَحِذْ. (عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَجْعَلَ», and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from سَبِيلٍ.

ukberi-tibyan:142-142.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الْمُنَافِقِينَ يُخَادِعُونَ اللَّهَ وَهُوَ خَادِعُهُمْ وَإِذَا قَامُوا إِلَى الصَّلَاةِ قَامُوا كُسَالَى يُرَاءُونَ النَّاسَ وَلَا يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا) (١٤٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَهُوَ خَادِعُهُمْ) and «كُسَالَى»: two aḥwāl (circumstantial expressions; sing. ḥāl). (يُرَاءُونَ): it is read with prolongation (madd) and lightening of the hamza, and it is read with the alif dropped and the hamza doubled (يُرَؤُّونَ), i.e. "they induce others to show off". Its position is accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in كُسَالَى; it may also be a badal (substitute) from كُسَالَى, and it may be resumptive. (إِلَّا قَلِيلًا): an adjective (naʿt) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) or of an omitted time.

ukberi-tibyan:143-143.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مُذَبْذَبِينَ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ لَا إِلَى هَؤُلَاءِ وَلَا إِلَى هَؤُلَاءِ وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُ سَبِيلًا) (١٤٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُذَبْذَبِينَ): it is accusative by way of censure (ʿalā al-dhamm). It is also said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يَذْكُرُونَ. The majority read the dhāl with fatḥa, as a passive (with the agent unnamed), i.e. their hypocrisy drove them to waver. It is also read with kasra on the second dhāl (مُذَبْذِبِينَ), i.e. "wavering". According to the Basrans the second dhāl is not a substitute; rather ذَبْذَبَ is a root in its own right.
The Kufans said: the original is ذَبَّبَ, and a dhāl was substituted for the first bāʾ. «ذَلِكَ» stands in the place of "the two of them" (بَيْنَهُمَا), i.e. between faith and disbelief, or between the Muslims and the Jews. (لَا إِلَى هَؤُلَاءِ وَلَا إِلَى هَؤُلَاءِ): «إِلَى» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, i.e. "they do not belong wholly to these, nor wholly to those". The position of (لَا إِلَى هَؤُلَاءِ) is accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in مُذَبْذَبِينَ, i.e. "they waver, changing colours".
[Translator's note: the printed text has ذَبَبَ without the doubling sign.]

ukberi-tibyan:145-145.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الْمُنَافِقِينَ فِي الدَّرْكِ الْأَسْفَلِ مِنَ النَّارِ وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُمْ نَصِيرًا) (١٤٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي الدَّرْكِ): it is read with fatḥa on the rāʾ and with it quiescent; they are two dialectal forms. And (مِنَ النَّارِ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الدَّرْك; what governs it is the notion of settledness (al-istiqrār). It may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in الْأَسْفَل.

ukberi-tibyan:146-146.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا وَأَصْلَحُوا وَاعْتَصَمُوا بِاللَّهِ وَأَخْلَصُوا دِينَهُمْ لِلَّهِ فَأُولَئِكَ مَعَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَسَوْفَ يُؤْتِ اللَّهُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا) (١٤٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا): in the position of the accusative as an exception from the genitive pronoun in His saying «وَلَنْ تَجِدْ لَهُمْ»; it may also be from His saying «فِي الدَّرْكِ». It is also said: it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is «فَأُولَئِكَ مَعَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ».

ukberi-tibyan:147-147.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَا يَفْعَلُ اللَّهُ بِعَذَابِكُمْ إِنْ شَكَرْتُمْ وَآمَنْتُمْ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ شَاكِرًا عَلِيمًا) (١٤٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا يَفْعَلُ اللَّهُ): concerning «مَا» there are two views. The sounder of them is that it is an interrogative in the position of the accusative governed by يَفْعَلُ, and (بِعَذَابِكُمْ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يَفْعَلُ. Second: that it is a negation, the implied wording being "Allah does nothing with your punishment", and the meaning is "He will not punish you".

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ وَأُولِي الْأَمْرِ مِنْكُمْ فَإِنْ تَنَازَعْتُمْ فِي شَيْءٍ فَرُدُّوهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَالرَّسُولِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ ذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَحْسَنُ تَأْوِيلًا) (٥٩).
His saying: (وَأُولِي الْأَمْرِ مِنْكُمْ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from أُولِي. [Translator's note: i.e. مِنْكُمْ is the ḥāl.] (تَأْوِيلًا): a tamyīz (specification).

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ يَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّهُمْ آمَنُوا بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَتَحَاكَمُوا إِلَى الطَّاغُوتِ وَقَدْ أُمِرُوا أَنْ يَكْفُرُوا بِهِ وَيُرِيدُ الشَّيْطَانُ أَنْ يُضِلَّهُمْ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا) (٦٠).
His saying: (وَيُرِيدُونَ) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has يُرِيدُونَ]: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الَّذِينَ يَزْعُمُونَ, or from the pronoun in يَزْعُمُونَ. (يَزْعُمُونَ) is one of the sisters of ظَنَنْتُ in requiring two objects, and «أَنَّ» with what it governs stands in place of both. (وَقَدْ أُمِرُوا): in the position of a ḥāl from the agent in يُرِيدُونَ. الطَّاغُوت is treated as feminine and as masculine; its pronoun here is masculine, and we have discussed it in al-Baqara. (أَنْ يُضِلَّهُمْ ضَلَالًا): i.e. "so that they go astray (فَيَضِلُّوا) a straying". ضَلَالًا may also mean إِضْلَالًا ("misleading"), one of the two maṣdars (verbal nouns) being put in place of the other.

ukberi-tibyan:61-61.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعَالَوْا إِلَى مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ وَإِلَى الرَّسُولِ رَأَيْتَ الْمُنَافِقِينَ يَصُدُّونَ عَنْكَ صُدُودًا) (٦١).
His saying: (تَعَالَوْا): the original is تَعَالَيُوا, and we have mentioned that in Āl ʿImrān. It is read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, with ḍamma on the lām [تَعَالُوا]; its justification is that the alif of تَعَالَى was dropped arbitrarily, then the lām was given ḍamma because of the wāw of the pronoun. (يَصُدُّونَ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). (صُدُودًا): a noun standing for the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), the maṣdar being صَدٌّ. It is also said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:62-62.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَكَيْفَ إِذَا أَصَابَتْهُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ ثُمَّ جَاءُوكَ يَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ إِنْ أَرَدْنَا إِلَّا إِحْسَانًا وَتَوْفِيقًا) (٦٢).
His saying: (فَكَيْفَ إِذَا أَصَابَتْهُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ): i.e. "then how will they act?". (يَحْلِفُونَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:63-63.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ مَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ وَعِظْهُمْ وَقُلْ لَهُمْ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ قَوْلًا بَلِيغًا) (٦٣).
His saying: (فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to قُلْ لَهُمْ. It is also said: it is attached to «بَلِيغًا», i.e. "reaching into their souls"; but this is weak, because an adjective does not govern what precedes it.

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا لِيُطَاعَ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ إِذْ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ جَاءُوكَ فَاسْتَغْفَرُوا اللَّهَ وَاسْتَغْفَرَ لَهُمُ الرَّسُولُ لَوَجَدُوا اللَّهَ تَوَّابًا رَحِيمًا) (٦٤).
His saying: (إِلَّا لِيُطَاعَ): in the accusative position as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), and the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَرْسَلْنَا.
(بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يُطَاعَ. It is also said: it is an object [governed through the preposition], i.e. "because of the command of Allah". (إِذْ ظَلَمُوا): an adverb (ẓarf), and what governs it is the khabar (predicate) of أَنَّ [Translator's note: the source has إِنَّ], namely «جَاءُوكَ». (وَاسْتَغْفَرَ لَهُمُ الرَّسُولُ): He did not say "and you asked forgiveness for them", because He turned from the second person to the third person, on account of what the overt noun conveys in indicating that he is the Messenger. (وَجَدُوا): transitive to two objects. It is also said: it is the one transitive to a single object. (تَوَّابًا): a ḥāl, and «رَحِيمًا» is a badal (substitute), or a ḥāl from the pronoun in تَوَّاب.

ukberi-tibyan:65-65.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ حَتَّى يُحَكِّمُوكَ فِيمَا شَجَرَ بَيْنَهُمْ ثُمَّ لَا يَجِدُوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ حَرَجًا مِمَّا قَضَيْتَ وَيُسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيمًا) (٦٥).
His saying: (فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ): there are two views. First: that the first «لَا» is redundant (zāʾida), the implied form being "so by your Lord, «لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ» (they do not believe)". It is also said: the second is redundant, and the oath is parenthetical between the negation and what is negated. The other view: that «لَا» negates something omitted, its implied form being "so no, they do not do [so]"; then He said: "By your Lord, they do not believe". (بَيْنَهُمْ): an adverb (ẓarf) for شَجَرَ, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَا» or from the agent of شَجَرَ. (ثُمَّ لَا يَجِدُوا): conjoined to يُحَكِّمُوكَ. (فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to يَجِدُوا as an adverbial phrase is attached to a verb. (حَرَجًا): the object of يَجِدُوا. فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ may also be a ḥāl from حَرَج. Both of these are on the basis that «يَجِدُوا» is the one transitive to a single object; it may also be the one transitive to two, with فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ as one of them. (مِمَّا قَضَيْتَ): an adjective of حَرَج, and so attached to something omitted. It may also be attached to حَرَج, because you say حَرِجْتُ مِنْ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ ("I felt constrained by this matter"). «مَا» may mean الَّذِي ("that which"), or be an indefinite qualified noun, or maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:66-68.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ أَنَّا كَتَبْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ أَنِ اقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ أَوِ اخْرُجُوا مِنْ دِيَارِكُمْ مَا فَعَلُوهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ مِنْهُمْ وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ فَعَلُوا مَا يُوعَظُونَ بِهِ لَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَهُمْ وَأَشَدَّ تَثْبِيتًا (٦٦) وَإِذًا لَآتَيْنَاهُمْ مِنْ لَدُنَّا أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا (٦٧) وَلَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ صِرَاطًا مُسْتَقِيمًا) (٦٨).
His saying: (أَنِ اقْتُلُوا): there are two views. First: it is maṣdariyya «أَنْ», the imperative is its ṣila, and the position of both is accusative by كَتَبْنَا.
Second: that «أَنْ» means the أَيْ ("that is") that explains a saying, and كَتَبْنَا is close in meaning to "We commanded" or "We said". (أَوِ اخْرُجُوا): read with kasra on the wāw, according to the basic rule for the meeting of two vowelless letters, and with ḍamma, in harmony with the ḍamma of the rāʾ, and because the wāw is of the same kind as the ḍamma. (مَا فَعَلُوهُ): the hāʾ is the pronoun of one of the two maṣdars (verbal nouns) of the two verbs, namely killing or going out; it may also be the pronoun of what was prescribed, the meaning [of the pronoun] being indicated by كَتَبْنَا. (إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ): read in the nominative as a badal (substitute) from the nominative pronoun, and the meaning supports it, because the meaning is "a few of them did it"; and in the accusative according to the basic rule of exception; the first is stronger. (مِنْهُمْ): an adjective of «قَلِيلٌ». (تَثْبِيتًا): a tamyīz (specification). (وَإِذَنْ): an answer to «لَوْ», cancelled (inoperative). (مِنْ لَدُنَّا): attached (mutaʿalliq) to آتَيْنَاهُمْ.
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أَجْرًا». (صِرَاطًا): a second object.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَآتُوا النِّسَاءَ صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ نِحْلَةً فَإِنْ طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ نَفْسًا فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا) (٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نِحْلَةً): a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of آتُوهُنَّ is "give them as a free gift" (أَنْحِلُوهُنَّ). It is also said: it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); on this view it may be a ḥāl from the agents, i.e. "giving freely", or from الصَّدُقَات, or from النِّسَاء, i.e. "given [them] freely". (نَفْسًا): a tamyīz (specification), and what governs it is طِبْنَ. The singular here is in the place of the plural, because the meaning is understood; what makes that good is that نَفْسًا here has a generic sense, so it became like دِرْهَمًا in your saying عِنْدِي عِشْرُونَ دِرْهَمًا ("I have twenty dirhams"). (فَكُلُوهُ): the hāʾ refers back to شَيْءٍ, and the hāʾ in مِنْهُ refers back to the wealth, because the dowries are wealth. (هَنِيئًا): a maṣdar that came on the pattern faʿīl; it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a wholesome eating". It is also said: it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl from the hāʾ, the implied form being "made wholesome" or "good".
(مَرِيئًا): like it. الْمَرِيءُ is faʿīl in the sense of mufʿil, because you say أَمْرَأَنِي الشَّيْءُ ("the thing agreed with me") when you do not use it together with هَنَأَنِي; but if you say هَنَأَنِي وَمَرَأَنِي [Translator's note: the text writes هَنَّانِي وَمَرَّانِي, without the hamza], you do not bring the hamza [of afʿala] in مَرَأَنِي, so that it follows هَنَأَنِي.

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تُؤْتُوا السُّفَهَاءَ أَمْوَالَكُمُ الَّتِي جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ قِيَامًا وَارْزُقُوهُمْ فِيهَا وَاكْسُوهُمْ وَقُولُوا لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفًا) (٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَمْوَالَكُمُ الَّتِي): the majority read الَّتِي in the singular, because the singular of الْأَمْوَال
is masculine; had He said اللَّوَاتِي, it would have been a plural just as الْأَمْوَال is a plural, and when an adjective is made plural because the noun it qualifies is plural, its singular is like the singular of the qualified noun in being masculine or feminine. It was read, among the irregular (shādhdh) readings, اللَّوَاتِي in the plural, taking account of the wording of الْأَمْوَال.
(جَعَلَ اللَّهُ): i.e. "made it into", so it is transitive to two objects, the first being omitted, namely the returning pronoun (al-ʿāʾid). It may also have the sense of "created", so that قِيَامًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(قِيَامًا): it is read with yāʾ and alif, and it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of قَامَ; the yāʾ is a substitute for the wāw, and it was substituted for it because [the wāw] was weakened in the verb and had a kasra before it. The implied sense is: "which Allah has made for you the means of the standing of your bodies", i.e. their survival.
It is also read قِيَمًا without alif, and there are three views on it. The first: that it is a maṣdar like الْحِوَل and الْعِوَض; the regular form would be for the wāw to be kept, since it is protected by being medial, as it remained sound in الْحِوَل and الْعِوَض; but they changed it into yāʾ by analogy with «قِيَام», given its weakening in the verb. The second: that it is the plural of قِيمَة ("value"), like دِيمَة and دِيَم; the meaning is that wealth is like the values of souls, since their survival depends on it. Abū ʿAlī said: this is not sound, because it has been read [قِيَمًا] in His saying: (دِينًا قِيَمًا مِلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ), and in His saying: (الْكَعْبَةَ الْبَيْتَ الْحَرَامَ قِيَامًا), and the meaning of "value" does not fit in either of them. The third view: that the origin is قِيَامًا and the alif was dropped, as it was dropped in خِيَمٌ.
It is also read قِوَامًا, with kasra on the qāf and with wāw and alif, and there are two views on it. The first: it is the maṣdar of قَاوَمْتُ قِوَامًا, like لَاوَذْتُ لِوَاذًا, so [the wāw] remained sound in the maṣdar since it remained sound in the verb. The second: that it is a noun for that by which an affair is upheld, and not a maṣdar. It is also read likewise but without alif (قِوَمًا), and it is a maṣdar whose medial radical (ʿayn) has remained sound and has come according to the original form, like الْعِوَض. It is also read with fatḥa on the qāf and with wāw and alif (قَوَامًا), and there are two views on it. The first: it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), like السَّلَام, الْكَلَام and الدَّوَام. The second: it is a dialectal variant of الْقِوَام, which means "stature"; one says جَارِيَةٌ حَسَنَةُ الْقَوَامِ وَالْقِوَامِ ("a girl of fine stature"); the implied sense is: "which Allah has made the means of the survival of your statures".
(وَارْزُقُوهُمْ فِيهَا): there are two views on it. The first: that «فِي» has its basic meaning, and the sense is: "make for them a provision in it". The second: that it has the sense of مِنْ ("from").

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَابْتَلُوا الْيَتَامَى حَتَّى إِذَا بَلَغُوا النِّكَاحَ فَإِنْ آنَسْتُمْ مِنْهُمْ رُشْدًا فَادْفَعُوا إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوَالَهُمْ وَلَا تَأْكُلُوهَا إِسْرَافًا وَبِدَارًا أَنْ يَكْبَرُوا وَمَنْ كَانَ غَنِيًّا فَلْيَسْتَعْفِفْ وَمَنْ كَانَ فَقِيرًا فَلْيَأْكُلْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ فَإِذَا دَفَعْتُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوَالَهُمْ فَأَشْهِدُوا عَلَيْهِمْ وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ حَسِيبًا) (٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حَتَّى إِذَا بَلَغُوا): حَتَّى here does not govern; it has entered upon the speech only for the meaning of limit (ghāya), as it enters upon the mubtadaʾ (subject). The apodosis (jawāb) of إِذَا is «فَإِنْ آنَسْتُمْ», and the apodosis of إِنْ is «فَادْفَعُوا»;
so what governs «إِذَا» is what is distilled from the meaning of its apodosis, the implied form being: "when they reach [marriageable age] being of sound judgement, then hand over".
(إِسْرَافًا وَبِدَارًا): two maṣdars (verbal nouns), objects of purpose (mafʿūl lahu). It is also said: they are two maṣdars in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being extravagant and hastening". الْبِدَار is the maṣdar of بَادَرْتُ, and it belongs to the category of mufāʿala that takes place between two parties, because the orphan is moving towards adulthood and the guardian is moving towards taking his wealth, so it is as though the two were racing each other.
It may also be "from one [party]". (أَنْ يَكْبَرُوا): the object of بِدَارًا, i.e. "hastening [against] their growing up".
(وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ): on the fāʿil (agent) of كَفَى there are two views. The first: it is the name of Allah, and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), having entered to indicate the sense of command, since the implied form is: "be content with Allah" (اكْتَفِ بِاللَّهِ). The second: that the agent is implied, and the implied form is: "contentment with Allah suffices", so on this view بِاللَّهِ is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (حَسِيبًا): a ḥāl; it is also said to be a tamyīz (specification). كَفَى is transitive to two objects, and both have been omitted here; the implied form is: "Allah suffices you against their evil", and the like. The proof of that is His saying: (فَسَيَكْفِيكَهُمُ اللَّهُ).

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِلرِّجَالِ نَصِيبٌ مِمَّا تَرَكَ الْوَالِدَانِ وَالْأَقْرَبُونَ وَلِلنِّسَاءِ نَصِيبٌ مِمَّا تَرَكَ الْوَالِدَانِ وَالْأَقْرَبُونَ مِمَّا قَلَّ مِنْهُ أَوْ كَثُرَ نَصِيبًا مَفْرُوضًا) (٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَلَّ مِنْهُ) [i.e. مِمَّا قَلَّ مِنْهُ]: it may be a badal (substitute) for «مِمَّا تَرَكَ»; and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted pronoun in تَرَكَ, i.e. "from what he left, little or much", or "being settled out of what is little".
(نَصِيبًا): it is said that it occupies the place of the maṣdar (verbal noun), and what governs it is the meaning of what precedes, since the implied form is "as a gift" or "as an entitlement".
It is also said: it is an emphasising ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), governed by the sense of settledness (istiqrār) in His saying «لِلرِّجَالِ نَصِيبٌ»; for that reason the ḥāl from it was good.
It is also said: it is a ḥāl from the agent in قَلَّ or كَثُرَ. It is also said: it is the object of an omitted verb, its implied form being: "He made a share obligatory for them". It is also said: it is accusative by an implied أَعْنِي ("I mean").

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا حَضَرَ الْقِسْمَةَ أُولُو الْقُرْبَى وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينُ فَارْزُقُوهُمْ مِنْهُ وَقُولُوا لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفًا) (٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَارْزُقُوهُمْ مِنْهُ): the pronoun refers back to what is divided (al-muqassam), because the mention of الْقِسْمَة indicates it [Translator's note: the text reads «عَدْلٌ عَلَيْهِ», evidently for «دَلَّ عَلَيْهِ», "indicates it"].

ukberi-tibyan:148-148.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا يُحِبُّ اللَّهُ الْجَهْرَ بِالسُّوءِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ إِلَّا مَنْ ظُلِمَ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ سَمِيعًا عَلِيمًا) (١٤٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِالسُّوءِ): the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the maṣdar (verbal noun), and concerning the position of the two [the preposition and its noun] there are two views. First: accusative, its implied form being "He does not love that you speak evil publicly". Second: nominative, its implied form being "that evil be spoken publicly". And (مِنَ الْقَوْلِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from السُّوء. (إِلَّا مَنْ ظُلِمَ): a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) in the position of the accusative. It is also said: it is joined (muttaṣil), the meaning being "He does not love that anyone speak evil publicly, except one who is wronged and so speaks publicly", i.e. he calls upon Allah to remove the evil that has befallen him, or complains of that to an imam or a ruler. On this view it may be in the position of the accusative, and it may be in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from the omitted [agent], since the implied wording is "that anyone speak publicly". It has also been read ظَلَمَ, with fatḥa on the ẓāʾ, with the agent named; it is then disjoined, the implied wording being "but the wrongdoer — for the one he wronged is given latitude to obtain redress from him"; this is a weak reading.

ukberi-tibyan:150-150.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْفُرُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَيُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يُفَرِّقُوا بَيْنَ اللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَيَقُولُونَ نُؤْمِنُ بِبَعْضٍ وَنَكْفُرُ بِبَعْضٍ وَيُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَتَّخِذُوا بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ سَبِيلًا) (١٥٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ سَبِيلًا): ذَلِكَ occurs with the meaning of the singular, the dual and the plural; here it has the meaning of the dual, i.e. بَيْنَهُمَا ("between the two").

ukberi-tibyan:151-151.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْكَافِرُونَ حَقًّا وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابًا مُهِينًا) (١٥١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حَقًّا): a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. حَقَّ ذَلِكَ حَقًّا ("that is truly true"). It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "those are the disbelievers, without doubt".

ukberi-tibyan:153-153.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَسْأَلُكَ أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ أَنْ تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ كِتَابًا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فَقَدْ سَأَلُوا مُوسَى أَكْبَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالُوا أَرِنَا اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ بِظُلْمِهِمْ ثُمَّ اتَّخَذُوا الْعِجْلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ فَعَفَوْنَا عَنْ ذَلِكَ وَآتَيْنَا مُوسَى سُلْطَانًا مُبِينًا) (١٣٥). [Translator's note: the verse number is printed as ١٣٥; this is verse ١٥٣.]
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَكْبَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ): i.e. "something greater", or "a request greater". (جَهْرَةً): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. مُجَاهِرِينَ ("openly"). It is also said: the implied wording is قَوْلًا جَهْرَةً ("an open saying"); and it is also said: رُؤْيَةً جَهْرَةً ("an open seeing").

ukberi-tibyan:154-154.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَهُمُ الطُّورَ بِمِيثَاقِهِمْ وَقُلْنَا لَهُمُ ادْخُلُوا الْبَابَ سُجَّدًا وَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ لَا تَعْدُوا فِي السَّبْتِ وَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُمْ مِيثَاقًا غَلِيظًا) (١٥٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَهُمُ): «فَوْقَهُمْ» may be an adverbial (ẓarf) for رَفَعْنَا, and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الطُّورَ». (بِمِيثَاقِهِمْ): in the position of the accusative, attached (mutaʿalliq) to رَفَعْنَا; its implied form is بِنَقْضِ مِيثَاقِهِمْ ("because of their breaking their covenant"), the meaning being "We raised the mountain above them to frighten them, because of their breaking the covenant". And (سُجَّدًا): a ḥāl. (لَا تَعْدُوا): it is read with the dāl light and the ʿayn quiescent; one says عَدَا يَعْدُو when someone transgresses the limit. It is also read with the dāl doubled and the ʿayn quiescent (لَا تَعْدُّوا); its original is تَعْتَدُوا, and the tāʾ was changed into dāl and assimilated. This is a weak reading, because it combines two quiescent letters, the second of which is not a letter of prolongation.
[Translator's note: the description of the first reading ("the ʿayn quiescent") is as printed; in the standard reading تَعْدُوا the ʿayn is indeed quiescent.]

ukberi-tibyan:155-155.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ مِيثَاقَهُمْ وَكُفْرِهِمْ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَقَتْلِهِمُ الْأَنْبِيَاءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَقَوْلِهِمْ قُلُوبُنَا غُلْفٌ بَلْ طَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهَا بِكُفْرِهِمْ فَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا) (١٥٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ): «مَا» is redundant (zāʾida). It is also said: it is a complete indefinite (nakira tāmma), and نَقْضِهِمْ is a badal (substitute) from it. Concerning what the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to there are two views. First: it is overt, namely His saying three verses later, (حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ); and His saying (فَبِظُلْمٍ) is a badal from His saying «فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ», the fāʾ being repeated in the badal because the separation grew long. Second: that what it is attached to is omitted, and there is evidence for it in the verse; the implied wording is "so because of their breaking their covenant, a seal was set upon their hearts", or "they were cursed". It is also said: the implied wording is "so because of their breaking their covenant they do not believe", the fāʾ being redundant. (بَلْ طَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهَا): i.e. "it is not as they claimed, that their hearts are vessels of knowledge". And (بِكُفْرِهِمْ): i.e. "because of their disbelief". The meaning may also be that their disbelief became a covering over their hearts, as you say طَبَعْتُ عَلَى الْكِيسِ بِالطِّينِ ("I sealed the purse with clay"), i.e. "I made it the seal". إِلَّا قَلِيلًا: i.e. "a little belief", or "a little time".

ukberi-tibyan:156-156.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَبِكُفْرِهِمْ وَقَوْلِهِمْ عَلَى مَرْيَمَ بُهْتَانًا عَظِيمًا) (١٥٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَبِكُفْرِهِمْ): conjoined to the first وَبِكُفْرِهِمْ. And (بُهْتَانًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) governed by الْقَوْل ("the saying"), because it is a kind of it; it is like their saying قَعَدَ الْقُرْفُصَاءَ ("he sat in the squatting posture"); so on this view it is equivalent to [a maṣdar of] the saying in being accusative. Some said: its implied form is قَوْلًا بُهْتَانًا ("a slanderous saying"). It is also said: the implied wording is بُهِتُوا بُهْتَانًا. It is also said: it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. مُبَاهِتِينَ ("slandering").

ukberi-tibyan:157-157.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَوْلِهِمْ إِنَّا قَتَلْنَا الْمَسِيحَ عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ وَلَكِنْ شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ لَفِي شَكٍّ مِنْهُ مَا لَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِلَّا اتِّبَاعَ الظَّنِّ وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ يَقِينًا) (١٥٧) (بَلْ رَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا) (١٥٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَقَوْلِهِمْ إِنَّا قَتَلْنَا): it is conjoined to وَكُفْرِهِمْ. And (عِيسَى): a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) from الْمَسِيح; and (رَسُولَ اللَّهِ) likewise.
(رَسُولَ اللَّهِ) may also be an adjective of عِيسَى, and it may be on the assumption of an implied أَعْنِي ("I mean").
(لَفِي شَكٍّ مِنْهُ): مِنْهُ is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of شَكٍّ; it is not permissible for it to be attached (mutaʿalliq) to شَكٍّ itself. The meaning is only "in doubt arising from it", i.e. from its direction, for one does not say شَكَكْتُ مِنْهُ ("I doubted from it"). If someone claims that مِنْ has the meaning of فِي, that is not sound in our view.
(مَا لَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ): the position of the negated clause may be genitive, as an emphasizing adjective of شَكٍّ, its implied form being "in a doubt about it, without knowledge". It may also be resumptive. مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida), and concerning the position of مِنْ عِلْمٍ there are two views. First: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what precedes it is the khabar (predicate); in this there are two views. First: [the khabar] is بِهِ, and «لَهُمْ» is an extra element (faḍla) that clarifies and specifies, like the one in His saying (وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ); on this view the [notion of] settledness is attached to it. Second: that لَهُمْ is the khabar, and on this view there are several views concerning بِهِ. First: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun latent in the khabar, what governs it being the [notion of] settledness. Second: that it is a ḥāl from الْعِلْم, because مِنْ is redundant and so does not prevent the ḥāl from being placed first — besides which, many of the Basrans permit placing the ḥāl of a genitive noun before it. Third: that it is by way of tabyīn (clarification), i.e. "they have no — I mean about it — [knowledge]"; it is not attached to عِلْم itself, because what a maṣdar (verbal noun) governs cannot precede it. The other view:
that the position of «مِنْ عِلْمٍ» is nominative as a fāʿil (agent), what governs it being the adverbial phrase, either لَهُمْ or بِهِ. (إِلَّا اتِّبَاعَ الظَّنِّ): an exception from a different kind. (وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ): the hāʾ is the pronoun of ʿĪsā. It is also said: it is the pronoun of the knowledge, i.e. "they did not kill the knowledge with certainty", as one says قَتَلْتُهُ عِلْمًا ("I mastered it thoroughly", literally "I killed it in knowledge"). And (يَقِينًا): an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. قَتْلًا يَقِينًا ("a certain killing") or عِلْمًا يَقِينًا ("a certain knowledge"). It may also be a maṣdar not from the wording of the verb but from its meaning, because the meaning of مَا قَتَلُوهُ is مَا عَمِلُوا ("they did not do"). [Translator's note: so in the printed text; presumably مَا عَلِمُوا, "they did not know", is intended.] It is also said: the implied wording is تَيَقَّنُوا ذَلِكَ يَقِينًا ("they were certain of that with certainty"). (بَلْ رَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ): the better course is to assimilate the lām into the rāʾ, because their point of articulation is one, and the rāʾ has trilling (takrīr), so it is stronger than the lām. The same does not hold for the rāʾ when it comes first, because assimilating it would remove the trilling in it. It has been read here with clear pronunciation (iẓhār).

ukberi-tibyan:69-69.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَنْ يُطِعِ اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ فَأُولَئِكَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ وَالصِّدِّيقِينَ وَالشُّهَدَاءِ وَالصَّالِحِينَ وَحَسُنَ أُولَئِكَ رَفِيقًا) (٦٩).
His saying: (مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الَّذِينَ, or from the genitive pronoun in عَلَيْهِمْ. (وَحَسُنَ): the majority read it with ḍamma on the sīn, and it was read with the sīn vowelless together with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ [وَحَسْنَ], as a lightening, just as they said عَضْدٌ for عَضُدٌ. «أُولَئِكَ» is its fāʿil (agent), and «رَفِيقًا» is a tamyīz (specification).
