It is also said: it is a ḥāl, and it is a singular in the place of a plural, i.e. "companions" (رُفَقَاءَ).

ukberi-tibyan:70-70.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ الْفَضْلُ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ عَلِيمًا) (٧٠).
His saying: (ذَلِكَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and there are two views on the khabar (predicate). First: «الْفَضْلُ», with «مِنَ اللَّهِ» a ḥāl (circumstantial), governed by the meaning of ذَلِكَ [i.e. the demonstrative sense]. Second: that الْفَضْلُ is an adjective, and مِنَ اللَّهِ is the khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:71-71.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا خُذُوا حِذْرَكُمْ فَانْفِرُوا ثُبَاتٍ أَوِ انْفِرُوا جَمِيعًا) (٧١).
His saying: (ثُبَاتٍ): the plural of ثُبَةٌ, which is a group; its original form is ثُبْوَةٌ, and its diminutive is ثُبَيَّةٌ. As for ثُبَةُ الْحَوْضِ, which is the middle of the cistern, its original form is ثَوْبَةٌ, from ثَابَ يَثُوبُ, said when something returns; its diminutive is ثُوَيْبَةٌ. «ثُبَاتٍ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise «جَمِيعًا».

ukberi-tibyan:72-72.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّ مِنْكُمْ لَمَنْ لَيُبَطِّئَنَّ فَإِنْ أَصَابَتْكُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ قَالَ قَدْ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيَّ إِذْ لَمْ أَكُنْ مَعَهُمْ شَهِيدًا) (٧٢).
His saying: (لَمَنْ): the noun (ism) of إِنَّ; it means الَّذِي ("the one who") or is an indefinite qualified noun. (لَيُبَطِّئَنَّ): a ṣila (relative clause) or an adjective, and مِنْكُمْ is the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ. «إِذْ لَمْ» is an adverb (ẓarf) for أَنْعَمَ.

ukberi-tibyan:73-73.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَئِنْ أَصَابَكُمْ فَضْلٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ لَيَقُولَنَّ كَأَنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُ مَوَدَّةٌ يَا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ مَعَهُمْ فَأَفُوزَ فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا) (٧٣).
His saying: (لَيَقُولَنَّ): with fatḥa on the lām, according to the wording of مَنْ; and it was read with ḍamma on it [لَيَقُولُنَّ], construed according to the meaning of مَنْ, which is plural. (كَأَنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ): it is lightened from the heavy (doubled) form [كَأَنَّ], and its noun is omitted, i.e. كَأَنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ, with yāʾ, because الْمَوَدَّة and الْوُدّ have the same meaning, and because the two have been separated; and it is read with tāʾ according to the wording of الْمَوَدَّة. It is a parenthetical statement between يَقُولُ and what is reported by it, namely His saying «يَا لَيْتَنِي»; the implied form being "he says: would that I…". It is also said: it is not parenthetical; rather it too is reported by يَقُولُ, i.e. he says: "as though there had been no…" and "would that I…". It is also said: كَأَنْ لَمْ with what is attached to it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in لَيَقُولَنَّ. (يَا لَيْتَنِي): the one addressed in the vocative is omitted, its implied form being "O people, would that I…". Abū ʿAlī says about this kind of construction: there is no omitted addressee in the phrase; rather «يَا» enters upon the verb, and the particle is for drawing attention. (فَأَفُوزَ): in the accusative as the answer to the wish, and in the nominative on the implied form "so I would (فَأَنَا) win".

ukberi-tibyan:74-74.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلْيُقَاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ الَّذِينَ يَشْرُونَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا بِالْآخِرَةِ وَمَنْ يُقَاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَيُقْتَلْ أَوْ يَغْلِبْ فَسَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا) (٧٤).
His saying: (أَوْ يَغْلِبْ فَسَوْفَ): the bāʾ is assimilated into the fāʾ, because both are from the two lips; some pronounced it distinctly.

ukberi-tibyan:75-75.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا لَكُمْ لَا تُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَالْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ وَالنِّسَاءِ وَالْوِلْدَانِ الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا أَخْرِجْنَا مِنْ هَذِهِ الْقَرْيَةِ الظَّالِمِ أَهْلُهَا وَاجْعَلْ لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ وَلِيًّا وَاجْعَلْ لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ نَصِيرًا) (٧٥).
His saying: (وَمَا لَكُمْ): مَا is interrogative, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and لَكُمْ is its khabar (predicate).
(لَا تُقَاتِلُونَ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and what governs it is the notion of settledness (al-istiqrār), as you say: مَا لَكَ قَائِمًا ("what is the matter with you, standing?"). (الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ): conjoined to the name of Allah, i.e. "and in the cause of the oppressed". Al-Mubarrad said: it is conjoined to السَّبِيل; but this is nothing. (الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ): in the genitive position, an adjective of the rational beings among those mentioned. It may also be accusative by an implied "I mean" (أَعْنِي). (الظَّالِمِ أَهْلُهَا): the alif and lām mean الَّتِي ("which"). The active participle was not made feminine, even though it is in wording an adjective of the town (الْقَرْيَة), because it has governed the overt noun mentioned, namely أَهْل; and every active participle, when it is applied to something other than the one it belongs to, is masculine or feminine according to the overt noun it governs.

ukberi-tibyan:77-77.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ قِيلَ لَهُمْ كُفُّوا أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ فَلَمَّا كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقِتَالُ إِذَا فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ يَخْشَوْنَ النَّاسَ كَخَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ أَوْ أَشَدَّ خَشْيَةً وَقَالُوا رَبَّنَا لِمْ كَتَبْتَ عَلَيْنَا الْقِتَالَ لَوْلَا أَخَّرْتَنَا إِلَى أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ قُلْ مَتَاعُ الدُّنْيَا قَلِيلٌ وَالْآخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ لِمَنِ اتَّقَى وَلَا تُظْلَمُونَ فَتِيلًا) (٧٧).
His saying: (إِذَا فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ): إِذَا here is the one of surprise (mufājaʾa), and the إِذَا of surprise is an adverb of place; an adverb of place in a construction like this may be the khabar (predicate) of the noun after it, which here is فَرِيقٌ; «مِنْهُمْ» is an adjective of فَرِيق, and «يَخْشَوْنَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); on this view what governs the adverb is the notion of settledness (al-istiqrār). إِذَا may also not be a khabar, so that فَرِيقٌ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), مِنْهُمْ its adjective, and يَخْشَوْنَ the khabar, which is what governs إِذَا. It is also said: إِذَا here is the temporal one; but this is nothing, because the temporal إِذَا is governed either by what precedes it or by what follows it. If it were governed by what precedes it, it would belong to its ṣila [Translator's note: the printed text reads كَانَتْ «مِنْ» صِلَتُهُ, i.e. "it would be part of its complement"]; and this is unsound here, because the implied form would become "so when fighting was prescribed for them at the time of fear, a party of them…", and this needs an apodosis for لَمَّا, and it has none. And if it were governed by what follows it, what governs it would be an apodosis to it, but إِذَا here has no apodosis; rather it is itself the apodosis of لَمَّا. (كَخَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ): i.e. "a fear like the fear of Allah", and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is put in construct with its object. (أَوْ أَشَدَّ): conjoined to الْخَشْيَة, and it is genitive [diptote, hence fatḥa]. It may also be accusative, conjoined to the position of the kāf. What is said about His saying أَشَدَّ خَشْيَةً is like what is said about His saying (أَوْ أَشَدَّ ذِكْرًا), and that has been mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَيْنَمَا تَكُونُوا يُدْرِكْكُمُ الْمَوْتُ وَلَوْ كُنْتُمْ فِي بُرُوجٍ مُشَيَّدَةٍ وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ حَسَنَةٌ يَقُولُوا هَذِهِ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ يَقُولُوا هَذِهِ مِنْ عِنْدِكَ قُلْ كُلٌّ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ فَمَالِ هَؤُلَاءِ الْقَوْمِ لَا يَكَادُونَ يَفْقَهُونَ حَدِيثًا) (٧٨).
His saying: (أَيْنَمَا): it is conditional here, and مَا is redundant (zāʾida); it frequently enters upon conditional أَيْنَ to strengthen its conditional meaning, and it may be omitted. «يُدْرِكْكُمُ» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). «يُدْرِكُكُمُ» has also been read in the nominative, which is irregular (shādhdh); its justification is that the fāʾ was omitted. (وَلَوْ كُنْتُمْ): in the sense of "and even if (وَإِنْ) you were", and this has been mentioned repeatedly. (قُلْ كُلٌّ): [كُلٌّ is] a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the muḍāf ilayhi is omitted, i.e. "all of that"; (مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ) is the khabar (predicate). (لَا يَكَادُونَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial). Some of the reciters pause on the lām in His saying مَا لِهَؤُلَاءِ, but it is not a place of pause; the lām in reality is connected to هَؤُلَاءِ, and it [the lām phrase] is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلْيَخْشَ الَّذِينَ لَوْ تَرَكُوا مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعَافًا خَافُوا عَلَيْهِمْ فَلْيَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَلْيَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا) (٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ): it may be an adverb (ẓarf) for تَرَكُوا, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ذُرِّيَّةً». (ضِعَافًا): it is read with tafkhīm (full pronunciation), according to the basic form, and with imāla (inclination of the vowel towards i) because of the kasra; that is permissible despite the elevated letter (ḥarf al-istiʿlāʾ) [ḍād], because it has kasra and comes first, so there is a descent in it. (خَافُوا): it is read with tafkhīm, according to the basic form, and with imāla, because the khāʾ takes kasra in some situations, namely خِفْتُ. It is the apodosis (jawāb) of لَوْ, and لَوْ has the meaning of إِنْ.

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوَالَ الْيَتَامَى ظُلْمًا إِنَّمَا يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ نَارًا وَسَيَصْلَوْنَ سَعِيرًا) (١٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ظُلْمًا): an object of purpose (mafʿūl lahu), or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). (فِي بُطُونِهِمْ نَارًا): something about it has been mentioned in al-Baqara; what is particular to this place is that فِي بُطُونِهِمْ is a ḥāl from نَارًا, i.e. "a fire being in their bellies", and it is not an adverb (ẓarf) for يَأْكُلُونَ. He [Abū ʿAlī] mentioned it in al-Tadhkira. (وَسَيَصْلَوْنَ): it is read with fatḥa on the yāʾ, its past tense being صَلَى النَّارَ يَصْلَاهَا ("he burned in the fire"); from it is His saying: (لَا يَصْلَاهَا إِلَّا الْأَشْقَى). It is read with ḍamma on it (وَسَيُصْلَوْنَ) as a verb whose agent is not named (passive), and it is read with doubling of the lām (وَسَيُصَلَّوْنَ) for intensiveness (taktīr).

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يُوصِيكُمُ اللَّهُ فِي أَوْلَادِكُمْ لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ فَإِنْ كُنَّ نِسَاءً فَوْقَ اثْنَتَيْنِ فَلَهُنَّ ثُلُثَا مَا تَرَكَ وَإِنْ كَانَتْ وَاحِدَةً فَلَهَا النِّصْفُ وَلِأَبَوَيْهِ لِكُلٍ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا السُّدُسُ مِمَّا تَرَكَ إِنْ كَانَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ وَلَدٌ وَوَرِثَهُ أَبَوَاهُ فَلِأُمِّهِ الثُّلُثُ فَإِنْ كَانَ لَهُ إِخْوَةٌ فَلِأُمِّهِ السُّدُسُ مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصِي بِهَا أَوْ دَيْنٍ آبَاؤُكُمْ وَأَبْنَاؤُكُمْ لَا تَدْرُونَ أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ لَكُمْ نَفْعًا فَرِيضَةً مِنَ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا) (١١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ): the clause is in the position of the accusative by يُوصِي, because the meaning is "He prescribes for you" or "He legislates concerning your children"; the implied form is: "concerning the matter of your children". (فَإِنْ كُنَّ): the pronoun is for the females left behind, i.e. "if the ones left behind are…", and the mention of الْأَوْلَاد indicates it. (فَوْقَ اثْنَتَيْنِ): an adjective of نِسَاءً, i.e. "more than two". (وَإِنْ كَانَتْ وَاحِدَةً): with the accusative, i.e. "if the heiress is one"; and with the nominative (وَاحِدَةٌ), on the view that كَانَ is complete (tāmma). (النِّصْفُ): with ḍamma and with kasra [on the nūn] (النُّصْفُ / النِّصْفُ), two dialectal forms, and it has been read with both. (فَلِأُمِّهِ): with ḍamma on the hamza, which is the basic form; and with kasra on it (فَلِإِمِّهِ), to harmonise with the kasra of the lām before it and the kasra of the mīm
after it. (وَإِنْ كَانُوا إِخْوَةً) [Translator's note: so quoted in the text; the verse reads فَإِنْ كَانَ لَهُ إِخْوَةٌ]: the plural here is for two, because two [siblings] reduce [the mother's share] according to the majority; according to Ibn ʿAbbās it is in its proper sense, and two do not reduce it. السُّدُس, الثُّلُث, الرُّبُع and الثُّمُن are with ḍamma on their middle letters, which is the good dialectal form; giving them sukūn is a [dialectal] form, and it has been read so.
(مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from السُّدُس, its implied form being: "being due after a bequest", the governing element being the adverbial phrase. It may also be an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "that is settled for them after the bequest has been paid out". An omitted muḍāf must be implied, because الْوَصِيَّة here is the wealth bequeathed. It is also said that الْوَصِيَّة may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), like الْفَرِيضَة.
(أَوْ دَيْنٍ): «أَوْ» is for one of two things, and it does not indicate order, since there is no difference between your saying جَاءَنِي زَيْدٌ أَوْ عَمْرٌو ("Zayd or ʿAmr came to me") and your saying جَاءَ عَمْرٌو أَوْ زَيْدٌ, because أَوْ is for one of two things, and a single thing has no order. By this is explained the saying of whoever said: the implied form is "after a debt or a bequest". Order arises only when the two are combined, in which case the debt is given precedence over the bequest.
(آبَاؤُكُمْ وَأَبْنَاؤُكُمْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject). (لَا تَدْرُونَ أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ لَكُمْ نَفْعًا): the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. أَيُّهُمْ is a mubtadaʾ and أَقْرَبُ its khabar, and the clause is in the position of the accusative by تَدْرُونَ; [the verb] is suspended (muʿallaq) from governing in wording because it is one of the verbs of the heart. (نَفْعًا): a tamyīz (specification). (فَرِيضَةً): the maṣdar of an omitted verb, i.e. "that has been prescribed as a prescription".

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَكُمْ نِصْفُ مَا تَرَكَ أَزْوَاجُكُمْ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُنَّ وَلَدٌ فَإِنْ كَانَ لَهُنَّ وَلَدٌ فَلَكُمُ الرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكْنَ مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصِينَ بِهَا أَوْ دَيْنٍ وَلَهُنَّ الرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكْتُمْ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَكُمْ وَلَدٌ فَإِنْ كَانَ لَكُمْ وَلَدٌ فَلَهُنَّ الثُّمُنُ مِمَّا تَرَكْتُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ تُوصُونَ بِهَا أَوْ دَيْنٍ وَإِنْ كَانَ رَجُلٌ يُورَثُ كَلَالَةً أَوِ امْرَأَةٌ وَلَهُ أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌ فَلِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا السُّدُسُ فَإِنْ كَانُوا أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَهُمْ شُرَكَاءُ فِي الثُّلُثِ مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصَى بِهَا أَوْ دَيْنٍ غَيْرَ مُضَارٍّ وَصِيَّةً مِنَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَلِيمٌ) (١٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِنْ كَانَ رَجُلٌ): on «كَانَ» there are two views:
The first: it is complete (tāmma) and رَجُلٌ is its fāʿil (agent); «يُورَثُ» is an adjective of it, and «كَلَالَةً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يُورَثُ. On this view الْكَلَالَة
is a noun for the deceased who has left neither child nor parent. Had it been read كَلَالَةٌ in the nominative, as an adjective, or as a badal (substitute) from the pronoun in يُورَثُ, it would have been permissible; however, I know of no one who read it so, and one reads only what has been transmitted [Translator's note: the text has «فَلَا يُقْرَآنِ», a dual form, here]. The second view: that كَانَ is the incomplete (nāqiṣa) one, رَجُلٌ its noun, يُورَثُ its khabar (predicate), and «كَلَالَةً» also a ḥāl.
It is also said: الْكَلَالَة is a noun for the inherited wealth; on this view «كَلَالَةً» is accusative as the second object of يُورَثُ, as you say وَرِثَ زَيْدٌ مَالًا ("Zayd inherited wealth"). It is also said: الْكَلَالَة is a noun for the heirs among whom there is neither child nor parent; on this view there is no way to account for this speech on the well-known reading, because there is nothing to make it accusative: do you not see that if you said زَيْدٌ يُورَثُ إِخْوَةً it would not be sound? It is only sound on the reading of whoever reads with kasra on the rāʾ, undoubled and doubled (يُورِثُ / يُوَرِّثُ), and it has been read with both. It is also said: this doctrine is sound if an omitted muḍāf is implied, its implied form being: "if a man is inherited from, being one who has kalāla" (ذَا كَلَالَةٍ), so ذَا is a ḥāl or the khabar of كَانَ. Whoever reads with kasra on the rāʾ makes كَلَالَةً a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and الْكَلَالَة is then either the heirs or the wealth; in both cases one of the two objects is omitted, the implied form being: "he leaves his family wealth as inheritance".
(وَلَهُ أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌ): if it is asked: the man and the woman have both been mentioned before, so why did He make the pronoun singular and masculine?
It is answered: as for its being singular, that is because «أَوْ» is for one of two things, and He said أَوِ امْرَأَةٌ, so He made the pronoun singular for that reason. As for its being masculine, there are three views on it. The first: it refers back to الرَّجُل, because it is masculine and mentioned first.
The second: that it refers back to "one of them" (أَحَدُهُمَا), and the word أَحَد is masculine. The third: that it refers back to the deceased or the one inherited from, because something indicating it has come before.
(فَإِنْ كَانُوا): the wāw is the pronoun of the siblings from the mother, who are indicated by His saying أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌ; (ذَلِكَ) is an allusion to the single one. (يُوصَى بِهَا): it is read with kasra on the ṣād (يُوصِي), i.e. "the dying person bequeaths it"; and with fatḥa on it, as a verb whose agent is not named (passive), and that has the meaning of the first reading; and it is read with doubling (يُوَصِّي / يُوَصَّى) for intensiveness (taktīr). (غَيْرَ مُضَارٍّ): a ḥāl from the agent pronoun in يُوصِي.
The majority read مُضَارٍّ with nunation, and the implied form is: "not causing harm to his heirs" [Translator's note: the text vowels it مَضَارٍّ here]. (وَصِيَّةً): the maṣdar (verbal noun) of an omitted verb, i.e. "Allah has enjoined that", and what indicates the omitted element is His saying غَيْرَ مُضَارٍّ. Al-Ḥasan read: «غَيْرَ مُضَارِّ وَصِيَّةٍ» in the genitive construct, and there are two views on it. The first: its implied form is "not harming the people of a bequest" or "the one entitled to a bequest", so the muḍāf was omitted. The second: its implied form is "not harming at the time of a bequest", so it was omitted; this is of the type of annexing an adjective to a time. Close to that is their saying هُوَ فَارِسُ حَرْبٍ ("he is a horseman of war"), i.e. a horseman in war; and one says هُوَ فَارِسُ زَمَانِهِ ("he is the horseman of his time"), i.e. in his time. Likewise the implied form for the reading is: "not causing harm at the time of the bequest" [Translator's note: the text again vowels it مَضَارٍّ here].

ukberi-tibyan:159-159.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنْ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ إِلَّا لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ وَيَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيدًا) (١٥٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِنْ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ): إِنْ has the meaning of «مَا» (negation); the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the mubtadaʾ is omitted, its implied form being وَمَا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ أَحَدٌ ("and there is no one of the People of the Book…").
It is also said: what is omitted is مَنْ, and a parallel of it has passed; however, assuming مَنْ here is far-fetched, because the exception comes after the noun is complete, and relative or qualified (mawṣūfa) مَنْ is not complete [without its clause]. (لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ): the response of an omitted oath. It is also said: it was made emphatic with it [the nūn] outside an oath, as occurs in negation and interrogation. The hāʾ in «مَوْتِهِ» refers back to the implied أَحَدٌ; it is also said: it refers back to ʿĪsā. (وَيَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ): an adverbial (ẓarf) for شَهِيدٍ; and what governs it may be يَكُونُ.

ukberi-tibyan:160-160.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَبِظُلْمٍ مِنَ الَّذِينَ هَادُوا حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ طَيِّبَاتٍ أُحِلَّتْ لَهُمْ وَبِصَدِّهِمْ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ كَثِيرًا) (١٦٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَبِظُلْمٍ): the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to حَرَّمْنَا; we have mentioned the ruling on the fāʾ before. (كَثِيرًا): i.e. "a great hindering", or "a long time".

ukberi-tibyan:161-161.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَخْذِهِمُ الرِّبَا وَقَدْ نُهُوا عَنْهُ وَأَكْلِهِمْ أَمْوَالَ النَّاسِ بِالْبَاطِلِ وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ مِنْهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا) (١٦١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَخْذِهِمُ) and (أَكْلِهِمْ): conjoined to صَدِّهِمْ, and all of them are attached (mutaʿalliq) to حَرَّمْنَا; the maṣdars (verbal nouns) are annexed to their agent. (وَقَدْ نُهُوا عَنْهُ): a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:162-162.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَكِنِ الرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ مِنْهُمْ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ وَالْمُقِيمِينَ الصَّلَاةَ وَالْمُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَاةَ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ أُولَئِكَ سَنُؤْتِيهِمْ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا) (١٦٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَكِنِ الرَّاسِخُونَ): الرَّاسِخُونَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject). And (فِي الْعِلْمِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to it. And (مِنْهُمْ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «الرَّاسِخُونَ». (وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ): conjoined to الرَّاسِخُونَ. Concerning the khabar (predicate) of الرَّاسِخُونَ there are two views. First: (يُؤْمِنُونَ), and this is the correct one. Second: it is His saying «أُولَئِكَ سَنُؤْتِيهِمْ». (وَالْمُقِيمِينَ): the reading of the majority is with the yāʾ, and there are several views about it. First: that it is accusative by way of praise (ʿalā al-madḥ), i.e. "and I mean those who establish [the prayer]"; this is the school of the Basrans, and this occurs only after the sentence is complete.
Second: that it is conjoined to مَا, i.e. "they believe in what was sent down to you and in those who establish [the prayer]", meaning the angels. It is also said: the implied wording is "and in the religion of those who establish [the prayer]", in which case they are the Muslims. Third: that it is conjoined to قَبْلِ, its implied form being "and from before those who establish [the prayer]"; «قَبْلِ» was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi was put in its place. Fourth: that it is conjoined to the kāf in «قَبْلِكَ». Fifth: that it is conjoined to the kāf in «إِلَيْكَ». Sixth: that it is conjoined to the hāʾ and mīm in مِنْهُمْ. These [last] three views are mistaken in our view, because they involve conjoining an overt noun to a pronoun without repeating the preposition.
As for (وَالْمُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَاةَ), there are several views on its being nominative. First: it is conjoined to الرَّاسِخُونَ. Second: it is conjoined to the pronoun in الرَّاسِخُونَ. Third: it is conjoined to the pronoun in الْمُؤْمِنُونَ. Fourth: it is conjoined to the pronoun in يُؤْمِنُونَ. Fifth: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. وَهُمُ الْمُؤْتُونَ ("and they are those who give"). Sixth: it is a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is (أُولَئِكَ سَنُؤْتِيهِمْ).
أُولَئِكَ is a mubtadaʾ and what follows it is the khabar; it may also be in the position of the accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "and We shall give those…".

ukberi-tibyan:163-163.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ كَمَا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى نُوحٍ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطِ وَعِيسَى وَأَيُّوبَ وَيُونُسَ وَهَارُونَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ وَآتَيْنَا دَاوُدَ زَبُورًا) (١٦٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَمَا أَوْحَيْنَا): the kāf is an adjective (naʿt) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and مَا is maṣdarī. مَا may also have the meaning of الَّذِي, in which case it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), its implied form being "We revealed to you the like of what We revealed to Nūḥ, of the affirmation of Allah's oneness and other things". And (مِنْ بَعْدِهِ): in the position of the accusative, attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَوْحَيْنَا. It is not permissible for it to be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from النَّبِيِّينَ, because adverbials of time are not ḥāls of concrete beings. «مِنْ» may also be attached to النَّبِيِّينَ. Concerning (يُونُسَ) there are several dialectal forms; the most eloquent is with ḍamma on the nūn and without hamza; fatḥa and kasra on it are also permissible,
with and without hamza. All these names are non-Arabic except الْأَسْبَاط, which is the plural of سِبْط ("tribe"). الزَّبُور is faʿūl from al-zubr, which is writing; and the most likely is that it is faʿūl in the sense of mafʿūl (passive), like الرَّكُوب ("the mount") and الْحَلُوب ("the milch animal"). [Translator's note: the first mention of the pattern is printed فَعَوْلٌ; the following sentence has فَعُولٌ.] It is also read with ḍamma on the zāy (زُبُورًا), and there are two views about it. First: it is the plural of زَبُورٍ with the augment dropped, like فَلْسٍ and فُلُوسٍ. Second: that it is a maṣdar, like الْقُعُود and الْجُلُوس, and the Book sent down to Dāwūd was named by it.

ukberi-tibyan:164-164.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَرُسُلًا قَدْ قَصَصْنَاهُمْ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَرُسُلًا لَمْ نَقْصُصْهُمْ عَلَيْكَ وَكَلَّمَ اللَّهُ مُوسَى تَكْلِيمًا) (١٦٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَرُسُلًا): accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being وَقَصَصْنَا رُسُلًا ("and We related [the stories of] messengers"). It may also be accusative by a verb indicated by أَوْحَيْنَا, i.e. وَأَمَرْنَا رُسُلًا ("and We commanded messengers"). His saying (قَدْ قَصَصْنَاهُمْ) and «لَمْ نَقْصُصْهُمْ» have no [grammatical position] on the first view, because it explains the governing verb; on the second view they are two adjectives. [Translator's note: the printed text reads وَلَا عِوَضٌ ("no compensation"), evidently for وَلَا مَوْضِعَ ("no position"); translated according to the evident sense.] And (تَكْلِيمًا): an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun) that removes [the possibility of] figurative meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:165-165.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رُسُلًا مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنْذِرِينَ لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَى اللَّهِ حُجَّةٌ بَعْدَ الرُّسُلِ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا) (١٦٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (رُسُلًا): it may be a badal (substitute) from the first, and it may be an object, i.e. أَرْسَلْنَا رُسُلًا ("We sent messengers"). It may also be a preparatory ḥāl (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa) for what follows it, as you say مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ رَجُلًا صَالِحًا ("I passed by Zayd, a righteous man"); and it may be by way of praise (ʿalā al-madḥ), i.e. أَعْنِي رُسُلًا ("I mean messengers"). The lām in «لِئَلَّا» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to what الرُّسُل indicates, i.e. "We sent them for that"; it may also be attached to مُنْذِرِينَ or مُبَشِّرِينَ, or to what the two of them indicate.
And {حُجَّةٌ} is the noun (ism) of كَانَ, and its khabar (predicate) is لِلنَّاسِ.
And (عَلَى اللَّهِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from حُجَّةٍ, the implied wording being "the people have an argument existing against Allah". The khabar may also be عَلَى اللَّهِ, with لِلنَّاسِ as a ḥāl. It is not permissible for عَلَى اللَّهِ to be attached to حُجَّةٍ, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). And (بَعْدَ): an adverbial (ẓarf) for حُجَّةٍ. It may also be an adjective of it, because maṣdars may be qualified by an adverbial of time, just as an adverbial of time may serve as their predicate.

ukberi-tibyan:166-166.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَكِنِ اللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ إِلَيْكَ أَنْزَلَهُ بِعِلْمِهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ يَشْهَدُونَ وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا) (١٦٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْزَلَهُ): it has no grammatical position. And (بِعِلْمِهِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ, i.e. "He sent it down known", or "He sent it down with His knowledge in it", i.e. what He knows. It may also be a ḥāl from the agent, i.e. "He sent it down knowing it". (وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ يَشْهَدُونَ): it may have no grammatical position, its status being like that of لَكِنِ اللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ; and it may be a ḥāl, i.e. "He sent it down while the angels bear witness to its truth".

ukberi-tibyan:168-168.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَظَلَمُوا لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ طَرِيقًا) (١٦٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ): the like of it has been discussed at His saying (وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ) and (مَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيَذَرَ).

ukberi-tibyan:169-169.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِلَّا طَرِيقَ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا وَكَانَ ذَلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرًا) (١٦٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا طَرِيقَ جَهَنَّمَ): an exception of the same kind as the first, because the first has a general meaning, being in the context of negation. And (خَالِدِينَ): an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara, circumstantial of a future state).

ukberi-tibyan:170-170.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ قَدْ جَاءَكُمُ الرَّسُولُ بِالْحَقِّ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَآمِنُوا خَيْرًا لَكُمْ وَإِنْ تَكْفُرُوا فَإِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا) (١٧٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَدْ جَاءَكُمُ الرَّسُولُ بِالْحَقِّ): بِالْحَقِّ is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "with the truth accompanying him", or "speaking the truth". It may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to جَاءَ, i.e. "he came for the sake of establishing the truth". And (مِنْ): a ḥāl from the ḥāl. It may also be attached to جَاءَ, i.e. "the Messenger came from Allah". (فَآمِنُوا خَيْرًا): its implied form, according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, is وَأْتُوا خَيْرًا ("and bring about something better"), so it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); because when He commanded them to believe, He intended to bring them out of one state and into what is better than it. It is also said: the implied wording is إِيمَانًا خَيْرًا ("a better belief"), so it is an adjective (naʿt) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun). It is also said: it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted كَانَ, i.e. يَكُنِ الْإِيمَانُ خَيْرًا ("belief will be better"); this is not permissible according to the Basrans, because كَانَ is not omitted together with its noun while its khabar remains, except where it is unavoidable. What makes this weaker still is that the implied [verb] would be the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an omitted condition, so that what is omitted would be both the condition and its apodosis. It is also said: it is a ḥāl. Like it is (انْتَهُوا خَيْرًا) in all its views.

ukberi-tibyan:171-172.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ لَا تَغْلُوا فِي دِينِكُمْ وَلَا تَقُولُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْحَقَّ إِنَّمَا الْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ وَكَلِمَتُهُ أَلْقَاهَا إِلَى مَرْيَمَ وَرُوحٌ مِنْهُ فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَلَا تَقُولُوا ثَلَاثَةٌ انْتَهُوا خَيْرًا لَكُمْ إِنَّمَا اللَّهُ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ سُبْحَانَهُ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا (١٧١) لَنْ يَسْتَنْكِفَ الْمَسِيحُ أَنْ يَكُونَ عَبْدًا لِلَّهِ وَلَا الْمَلَائِكَةُ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ وَمَنْ يَسْتَنْكِفْ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِ وَيَسْتَكْبِرْ فَسَيَحْشُرُهُمْ إِلَيْهِ جَمِيعًا) (١٧٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَا تَقُولُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْحَقَّ): الْحَقَّ is the object of تَقُولُوا, i.e. "do not say anything but the true saying", because it has the meaning of "do not mention" and "do not believe". The saying here is what a clause expresses in your saying قُلْتُ زَيْدٌ مُنْطَلِقٌ ("I said: Zayd is leaving"). It may also be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun). And (الْمَسِيحُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject); (عِيسَى): a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); and (رَسُولُ اللَّهِ): its khabar (predicate). (وَكَلِمَتُهُ): conjoined to رَسُولٍ. And (أَلْقَاهَا): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), with قَدْ implied with it. Concerning what governs the ḥāl there are three views. First: the meaning of كَلِمَتِهِ, because the meaning of describing ʿĪsā as "the word" is that he was brought into being by the word, without a father; so it is as though He said "and the one He originated and brought forth". Second: that the implied wording is إِذْ كَانَ أَلْقَاهَا ("when He had cast it"), so إِذْ is an adverbial (ẓarf) for الْكَلِمَة, [Translator's note: the printed text has فَإِذَا here; the context indicates إِذْ.]
كَانَ is complete (tāmma), and أَلْقَاهَا is a ḥāl from the agent of كَانَ; this is like their saying ضَرْبِي زَيْدًا قَائِمًا ("my striking Zayd [is when he is] standing"). Third: that it is a ḥāl from the genitive hāʾ, what governs it being the meaning of the annexation, its implied form being "and the word of Allah, He casting it".
(وَرُوحٌ مِنْهُ): also conjoined to the khabar. And (ثَلَاثَةٌ): the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "our god is three" or "God is three". (إِنَّمَا اللَّهُ): a mubtadaʾ, and (إِلَهٌ) its khabar, and (وَاحِدٌ) a tawkīd (emphasis). (أَنْ يَكُونَ): i.e. مِنْ أَنْ يَكُونَ or عَنْ أَنْ يَكُونَ ("[far exalted] above having"); parallels of it have passed. Like it is (لَنْ يَسْتَنْكِفَ الْمَسِيحُ أَنْ يَكُونَ).
(وَلَا الْمَلَائِكَةُ): conjoined to الْمَسِيح; there is an omission in the phrase, i.e. "that they be servants".
